question: For each building at MIT that is used as a residence, list the building key, the total assignable area from building history records, and the number of history records for that building, but only include buildings whose total assignable area in history is more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean total assignable area across all buildings. For each building, also include a grand total row for the total assignable area and total number of history records across all such buildings. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH stats AS ( SELECT AVG(ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS mean_area, STDDEV(ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS stddev_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST ), res_buildings AS ( SELECT fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, SUM(fbh.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS total_assignable_area, COUNT(*) AS num_history_records FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND fb.SITE = 'MIT' GROUP BY fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ) SELECT rb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, rb.total_assignable_area, rb.num_history_records FROM res_buildings rb CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE rb.total_assignable_area > s.mean_area + s.stddev_area ) SELECT FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, total_assignable_area, num_history_records FROM inner_cte UNION ALL SELECT NULL AS FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, SUM(total_assignable_area) AS total_assignable_area, SUM(num_history_records) AS num_history_records FROM inner_cte ;
sub_questions: For each building that is used as a residence, give the building key and the total assignable area from building history records, for buildings whose total assignable area in history is more than one standard deviation above the mean total assignable area across all buildings, and restrict the results to buildings at MIT.
sub_sqls: WITH stats AS ( SELECT AVG(ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS mean_area, STDDEV(ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS stddev_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST ), res_buildings AS ( SELECT fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, SUM(fbh.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS total_assignable_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND fb.SITE = 'MIT' GROUP BY fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ) SELECT rb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, rb.total_assignable_area FROM res_buildings rb CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE rb.total_assignable_area > s.mean_area + s.stddev_area ;

question: For each department and academic year where the number of enrolled students in a subject is greater than 0, and the department is either Chemistry or Biology, provide the count of subjects, the minimum start date of the term, and indicate whether the subject count is above, below, or within 10% of the average subject count for that department across all academic years. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS academic_year, COUNT(DISTINCT tso.SUBJECT_ID) AS subject_count, MIN(ata.TERM_START_DATE) AS min_term_start_date FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON tso.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE WHERE tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology') GROUP BY tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR ), dept_avg AS ( SELECT department, AVG(subject_count) AS avg_subject_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY department ) SELECT i.department, i.academic_year, i.subject_count, i.min_term_start_date, d.avg_subject_count, CASE WHEN i.subject_count > d.avg_subject_count * 1.1 THEN 'ABOVE_AVERAGE' WHEN i.subject_count < d.avg_subject_count * 0.9 THEN 'BELOW_AVERAGE' ELSE 'WITHIN_10_PERCENT' END AS subject_count_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN dept_avg d ON i.department = d.department ORDER BY i.department, i.academic_year;
domain_knowledge: "biology and chemistry department" is predicated by "TABLE.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology')"
sub_questions: For each department and academic year where the number of enrolled students in a subject is greater than 0, and the department is either Chemistry or Biology, provide the count of subjects and the minimum start date of the term.
sub_sqls: SELECT tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS academic_year, COUNT(DISTINCT tso.SUBJECT_ID) AS subject_count, MIN(ata.TERM_START_DATE) AS min_term_start_date FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON tso.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE WHERE tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology') GROUP BY tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR;

question: For each department and academic year where the subject enrollment number is greater than 10 and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique subjects, the minimum total units offered, and the latest term end date for those subjects. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(DISTINCT ss.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_unique_subjects, MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units, at.TERM_CODE FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME WHERE cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ss.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER > 10 GROUP BY cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.TERM_CODE ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, inner_cte.num_unique_subjects, inner_cte.min_total_units, MAX(at.TERM_END_DATE) AS latest_term_end_date FROM inner_cte JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON inner_cte.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE GROUP BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, inner_cte.num_unique_subjects, inner_cte.min_total_units
sub_questions: For each department and academic year where the subject enrollment number is greater than 10 and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique subjects and the minimum total units offered.
sub_sqls: SELECT cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(DISTINCT ss.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_unique_subjects, MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME WHERE cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ss.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER > 10 GROUP BY cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR

question: For each department, what is the department name, the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department, and the school name, considering only departments that offer more than five subjects, are degree granting, and specifically include the Mathematics department (Course 18)? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ccso.SUBJECT_ID) > 5 OR sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.stddev_total_units, sd.SCHOOL_NAME FROM inner_cte ic LEFT JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name and the standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, considering only departments that offer more than five subjects, are degree granting, and specifically include the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ccso.SUBJECT_ID) > 5 OR sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ORDER BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For each course offered by a degree-granting department in the School of Engineering (excluding the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science department), what is the course key, course name, department name, the number of catalog subjects, the total units for those subjects, and only include those courses where the total units for those subjects is greater than the average total units for all such courses in the 2007 academic year? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT scd.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY, scd.COURSE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(ccc.SUBJECT_ID) AS subject_count, SUM(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON scd.DEPARTMENT = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND ccc.ACADEMIC_YEAR = '2007' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' GROUP BY scd.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY, scd.COURSE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY, COURSE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, subject_count, total_units FROM inner_cte WHERE total_units > (SELECT AVG(total_units) FROM inner_cte);

"except Cambridge-MIT Institute" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_NAME NOT IN ('CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST')"

question: For each department in the School of Engineering (excluding the Political Science department), provide the department code, department name, department full name, the number of subjects offered, the total number of enrolled students in those subjects during the 2019FA term, and the subject with the highest enrollment in each department, along with its subject title and enrollment count. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, COUNT(tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY) AS subject_count, SUM(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrollment FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN STUDENT_DEPARTMENT std ON tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = std.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE tso.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '17' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, ic.subject_count, ic.total_enrollment, tso.SUBJECT_ID AS highest_enrolled_subject_id, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE AS highest_enrolled_subject_title, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS AS highest_enrollment FROM inner_cte ic LEFT JOIN ( SELECT tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, tso.SUBJECT_ID, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE ORDER BY tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS DESC) AS rn FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso WHERE tso.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE <> '17' ) tso ON ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE AND tso.rn = 1 ORDER BY ic.total_enrollment DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, provide the department code, department name, department full name, the number of subjects offered, and the total number of enrolled students in subjects offered by that department in the School of Engineering during the 2019FA term, but exclude the Political Science department (department code '17').
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, COUNT(tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY) AS subject_count, SUM(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrollment FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN STUDENT_DEPARTMENT std ON tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = std.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE tso.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '17' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME;

question: For buildings in the WEST campus sector with an access level code of 2 that are academic buildings (excluding those used as a residence), what is the minimum area of any room and the total number of rooms in those buildings, along with the full building name and the city where each building is located? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIN(fr.AREA) AS min_room_area, SUM(fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS) AS total_num_of_rooms, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY FROM FCLT_BUILDING fb JOIN FCLT_ROOMS fr ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.CAMPUS_SECTOR = 'WEST' AND fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE = 2 AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE <> 'RESIDENT' GROUP BY fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ) SELECT i.min_room_area, i.total_num_of_rooms, fb.BUILDING_NAME_LONG, fba.CITY FROM inner_cte i JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON i.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY LEFT JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
domain_knowledge: "used as a residence" is predicated by "TABLE.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT'"
sub_questions: What is the minimum area of any room and the total number of rooms in buildings located in the WEST campus sector, with an access level code of 2, and that are academic buildings, excluding buildings used as a residence?
sub_sqls: SELECT MIN(fr.AREA) AS min_room_area, SUM(fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS) AS total_num_of_rooms FROM FCLT_BUILDING fb JOIN FCLT_ROOMS fr ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.CAMPUS_SECTOR = 'WEST' AND fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE = 2 AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE <> 'RESIDENT' ;

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding Political Science, Course 17) that offers at least one subject with more than 0 enrolled students, show the department name, the number of unique students named "Zoe" enrolled in their offered subjects, the average number of unique students named "Zoe" per department as a benchmark, and categorize each department as 'HIGH_ENROLLMENT' (at least 10% more than the average), 'LOW_ENROLLMENT' (at least 10% less than the average), or 'AVERAGE'. List the top 10 departments by the number of unique students named "Zoe". Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT msd.FULL_NAME) AS unique_students FROM MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON msd.DEPARTMENT = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND msd.FIRST_NAME = 'Zoe' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '17' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.unique_students, avg_stats.avg_unique_students AS benchmark, CASE WHEN inner_cte.unique_students > avg_stats.avg_unique_students * 1.1 THEN 'HIGH_ENROLLMENT' WHEN inner_cte.unique_students < avg_stats.avg_unique_students * 0.9 THEN 'LOW_ENROLLMENT' ELSE 'AVERAGE' END AS enrollment_category FROM inner_cte CROSS JOIN ( SELECT AVG(unique_students) AS avg_unique_students FROM inner_cte ) avg_stats ORDER BY inner_cte.unique_students DESC LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: List the top 10 degree-granting departments by the number of unique students named "Zoe" enrolled in their offered subjects, showing the department name and the count of unique student full names, for departments that have at least one subject with more than 0 enrolled students and are not the Political Science department (Course 17).
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT msd.FULL_NAME) AS unique_students FROM MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON msd.DEPARTMENT = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND msd.FIRST_NAME = 'Zoe' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '17' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY unique_students DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each academic year, what is the academic year description, the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units of all subjects offered in that year by the Mathematics department (considering only years with more than 10 subjects), and the number of Mathematics subjects in the library reserve for that year? Also, include the term description for each academic year. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, STDDEV(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON ccso.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ccso.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC HAVING COUNT(ccso.SUBJECT_ID) > 10 ) SELECT icte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, icte.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, icte.stddev_total_units, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION, COUNT(DISTINCT lrm.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_math_subjects_in_library_reserve FROM inner_cte icte JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON icte.ACADEMIC_YEAR = ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR LEFT JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON ccso.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' LEFT JOIN LIBRARY_RESERVE_MATRL_DETAIL lrm ON lrm.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE AND lrm.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID GROUP BY icte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, icte.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION, icte.stddev_total_units ORDER BY icte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the academic year description and the standard deviation of the total units of all subjects offered in that year by the Mathematics department, considering only years with more than 10 subjects?
sub_sqls: SELECT ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, STDDEV(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON ccso.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ccso.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC HAVING COUNT(ccso.SUBJECT_ID) > 10 ORDER BY ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR;

question: For each department in the 'Engineering' school, what is the department name, the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department, and the average number of enrolled students for those subjects, considering only departments with more than 5 subjects, and only for the department 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' (Course 6)? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV(TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SUBJECT_SUMMARY WHERE SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.stddev_total_units, AVG(ss.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER) AS avg_enrollment FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME = ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME WHERE ss.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.stddev_total_units
domain_knowledge: "Computer Science" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
"Course 6" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name and the standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, considering only departments with more than 5 subjects, where the school name is 'Engineering', and the department is 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' (Course 6)?
sub_sqls: SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV(TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SUBJECT_SUMMARY WHERE SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ;

question: For each department, list the department name, the range and variance of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the academic year 2022 (excluding Political Science and only including degree-granting departments), and for each department, show only those subjects whose total units are above the average total units for that department in 2022. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SCD.DEPARTMENT_NAME, CCSO.SUBJECT_CODE, CCSO.TOTAL_UNITS FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION SCD JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED CCSO ON SCD.COURSE = CCSO.SUBJECT_CODE WHERE CCSO.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND SCD.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SCD.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Political Science' ) , dept_avg AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_units FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(i.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(i.TOTAL_UNITS) AS units_range, VARIANCE(i.TOTAL_UNITS) AS units_variance, i.SUBJECT_CODE, i.TOTAL_UNITS FROM inner_cte i JOIN dept_avg d ON i.DEPARTMENT_NAME = d.DEPARTMENT_NAME WHERE i.TOTAL_UNITS > d.avg_units GROUP BY i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.SUBJECT_CODE, i.TOTAL_UNITS ORDER BY i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, units_range DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and calculate the range and variance of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the academic year 2022, but only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the Political Science department.
sub_sqls: SELECT SCD.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(CCSO.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(CCSO.TOTAL_UNITS) AS units_range, VARIANCE(CCSO.TOTAL_UNITS) AS units_variance FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION SCD JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED CCSO ON SCD.COURSE = CCSO.SUBJECT_CODE WHERE CCSO.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND SCD.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SCD.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Political Science' GROUP BY SCD.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY units_range DESC;

question: For subjects offered in the academic year 2024 with total units equal to 12 in the Mathematics department, show the department code, department name, subject code, subject number, subject title, total units, and the name of the responsible faculty member. Assign row numbers within each department ordered by subject code. Only include subjects from the Mathematics department, and only include those where the responsible faculty member's name starts with 'H' (case insensitive). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE, t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.SUBJECT_CODE, t1.SUBJECT_NUMBER, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.TOTAL_UNITS, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY t1.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column, t1.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t1.TOTAL_UNITS = 12 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_CODE, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.SUBJECT_CODE, inner_cte.SUBJECT_NUMBER, inner_cte.SUBJECT_TITLE, inner_cte.TOTAL_UNITS, inner_cte.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE UPPER(inner_cte.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME) LIKE 'H%';
sub_questions: For subjects offered in the academic year 2024 with total units equal to 12 in the Mathematics department, show the department code, department name, subject code, subject number, subject title, total units, and assign row numbers within each department ordered by subject code. Only include subjects from the Mathematics department.

question: For students whose department is '6' and whose department name is 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci', show their first name, last name, department name, student year, the corresponding department's full name, the administrative department name, and, for each school, the total number of such students in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows grouped by the school name and ordered by the student's first name. sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t1.FIRST_NAME, t1.LAST_NAME, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.STUDENT_YEAR, t0.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, t2.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT t2 ON t1.DEPARTMENT = t2.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.DEPARTMENT = '6' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' ) SELECT icte.FIRST_NAME, icte.LAST_NAME, icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, icte.STUDENT_YEAR, icte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, icte.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(*) OVER ( PARTITION BY t0.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY icte.FIRST_NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_student_count FROM inner_cte icte JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 ON icte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME = t0.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME ORDER BY icte.FIRST_NAME;

sub_questions: For students whose department is '6' and whose department name is 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci', show their first name, last name, department name, student year, the corresponding department's full name, the administrative department name, and the average department phone number in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows grouped by the administrative department name and ordered by the student's first name.

question: For all subjects offered in the academic year 2024 by the Mathematics department, show the subject code, subject title, term description, and the number of subjects offered in the same term as each subject. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION, t0.TERM_CODE FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) SELECT i.SUBJECT_CODE, i.SUBJECT_TITLE, i.TERM_DESCRIPTION, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inner_cte ic WHERE ic.TERM_CODE = i.TERM_CODE) AS subjects_in_same_term FROM inner_cte i;
sub_questions: For all subjects offered in the academic year 2024 by the Mathematics department, show the subject code, subject title, term description, and the rank of each subject within its term description group ordered by subject code.
sub_sqls: SELECT t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION ORDER BY t0.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each academic year, what is the total number of lecture units for all subjects offered in regular terms by the Mathematics department (Course 18), and how does this total compare to the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all years? For each year, also indicate whether it is a 'HIGH_PERFORMER' (total lecture units at least one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean), 'LOW_PERFORMER' (at least one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) below the mean), or 'AVERAGE' (within one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the mean). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT at_all.ACADEMIC_YEAR, SUM(ccso.LECTURE_UNITS) AS total_lecture_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL at_all JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON at_all.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON at.TERM_CODE = ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE at.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY at_all.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) SELECT inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, inner_cte.total_lecture_units, stats.avg_lecture_units, stats.stddev_lecture_units, CASE WHEN inner_cte.total_lecture_units >= stats.avg_lecture_units + stats.stddev_lecture_units THEN 'HIGH_PERFORMER' WHEN inner_cte.total_lecture_units <= stats.avg_lecture_units - stats.stddev_lecture_units THEN 'LOW_PERFORMER' ELSE 'AVERAGE' END AS performance_category FROM inner_cte CROSS JOIN ( SELECT AVG(total_lecture_units) AS avg_lecture_units, STDDEV(total_lecture_units) AS stddev_lecture_units FROM inner_cte ) stats;
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the total number of lecture units for all subjects offered in terms that are regular terms and are offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18), considering only those academic years where the total lecture units are more than one standard deviation above the mean total lecture units across all academic years?
sub_sqls: SELECT at_all.ACADEMIC_YEAR, SUM(ccso.LECTURE_UNITS) AS total_lecture_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL at_all JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON at_all.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON at.TERM_CODE = ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE at.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY at_all.ACADEMIC_YEAR HAVING SUM(ccso.LECTURE_UNITS) > ( SELECT AVG(total_lecture_units) + STDDEV(total_lecture_units) FROM ( SELECT SUM(ccso2.LECTURE_UNITS) AS total_lecture_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL at_all2 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at2 ON at_all2.TERM_CODE = at2.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso2 ON at2.TERM_CODE = ccso2.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE at2.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' AND ccso2.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY at_all2.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) t );

question: For each department and academic year where the subject enrollment number is greater than 10 and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique subjects, the minimum total units offered, and indicate whether the minimum total units is above or below the average total units for that department and year ('ABOVE_AVERAGE' if above, 'BELOW_AVERAGE' if below, otherwise 'AVERAGE'). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(DISTINCT ss.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_unique_subjects, MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME WHERE cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ss.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER > 10 GROUP BY cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ), avg_units_cte AS ( SELECT cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME WHERE cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ss.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER > 10 GROUP BY cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) SELECT i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.ACADEMIC_YEAR, i.num_unique_subjects, i.min_total_units, a.avg_total_units, CASE WHEN i.min_total_units > a.avg_total_units THEN 'ABOVE_AVERAGE' WHEN i.min_total_units < a.avg_total_units THEN 'BELOW_AVERAGE' ELSE 'AVERAGE' END AS min_units_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN avg_units_cte a ON i.DEPARTMENT_NAME = a.DEPARTMENT_NAME AND i.ACADEMIC_YEAR = a.ACADEMIC_YEAR;
sub_questions: For each department and academic year where the subject enrollment number is greater than 10 and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique subjects and the minimum total units offered.
sub_sqls: SELECT cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(DISTINCT ss.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_unique_subjects, MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME WHERE cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ss.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER > 10 GROUP BY cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR

question: For each school and term, provide the term code, school name, the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of students enrolled in subjects offered in regular terms by the Chemistry or Biology departments. Include subtotals for each school (the corresponding school field is 'SUBTOTAL') and a grand total across all schools (the corresponding school field is 'TOTAL'). Do not repeat the term code if it is the same as the previous row. Sort the table by term code and school name. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE, TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS ON TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE WHERE ACADEMIC_TERMS.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' AND TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology') ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(term_code) OVER (ORDER BY term_sort, school_sort) = term_code THEN NULL ELSE term_code END AS term_code, school, avg_enrollment, enrollment_stddev FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(TERM_CODE) = 1 AND GROUPING(OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE TERM_CODE END AS term_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(TERM_CODE) = 0 AND GROUPING(OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME) = 1 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(TERM_CODE) = 1 AND GROUPING(OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME END AS school, CASE WHEN GROUPING(OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME) = 0 AND GROUPING(TERM_CODE) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME END AS school_sort, TERM_CODE AS term_code, AVG(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrollment, STDDEV(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrollment_stddev FROM inner_cte GROUP BY TERM_CODE, OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME WITH ROLLUP ) tbl ORDER BY term_sort, school_sort;
domain_knowledge: "biology and chemistry department" is predicated by "TABLE.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology')"
sub_questions: For each school, provide the school name and calculate the average and standard deviation of the number of students enrolled in its offered subjects, considering only subjects offered in regular terms and only for subjects offered by the Chemistry or Biology departments.
sub_sqls: SELECT OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrollment, STDDEV(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrollment_stddev FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS ON TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE WHERE ACADEMIC_TERMS.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' AND TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology') GROUP BY OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY enrollment_stddev DESC;

question: Among all degree-granting departments, which department has the highest average number of unique subject codes per course, and what is the department name, the average, and the total number of courses considered? Show only the top department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, cd.DEPARTMENT, cd.COURSE, COUNT(DISTINCT sc.SUBJECT_CODE) AS subject_count FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION cd ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = cd.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE sc ON cd.DEPARTMENT = sc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE cd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, cd.DEPARTMENT, cd.COURSE ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(ic.subject_count) AS avg_subject_codes_per_course, COUNT(ic.COURSE) AS total_courses FROM inner_cte ic GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY avg_subject_codes_per_course DESC LIMIT 1;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name, and what are the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of unique subject codes per course offered by that department, considering only degree-granting courses in the Mathematics department?
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(subject_count) - MIN(subject_count) AS subject_count_range, VARIANCE(subject_count) AS subject_count_variance, STDDEV(subject_count) AS subject_count_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION cd ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = cd.DEPARTMENT JOIN ( SELECT cd.COURSE, cd.DEPARTMENT, COUNT(DISTINCT sc.SUBJECT_CODE) AS subject_count FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION cd JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE sc ON cd.DEPARTMENT = sc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE cd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' GROUP BY cd.COURSE, cd.DEPARTMENT ) course_subject_stats ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = course_subject_stats.DEPARTMENT WHERE d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY subject_count_range DESC;

question: For each degree-granting department with a non-null department budget code, what is the highest number of associated administrative departments among all departments? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS admin_dept_count FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT a ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(admin_dept_count) AS max_admin_dept_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: List the top 10 department names along with the number of associated administrative departments, considering only departments that are degree granting, have a non-null department budget code, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS admin_dept_count FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT a ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY admin_dept_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each school, what is the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the clearing cost collector values for all associated administrative departments, considering only schools that have at least one degree granting department that is not the Mathematics department (Course 18)? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.SCHOOL_NAME, d.SCHOOL_CODE, AVG(a.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS avg_clearing_cost_collector, VARIANCE(a.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS clearing_cost_collector_variance, STDDEV(a.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS clearing_cost_collector_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT a ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Mathematics' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE != '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.SCHOOL_NAME, d.SCHOOL_CODE ) SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE, AVG(avg_clearing_cost_collector) AS school_avg_clearing_cost_collector, VARIANCE(avg_clearing_cost_collector) AS school_clearing_cost_collector_variance, STDDEV(avg_clearing_cost_collector) AS school_clearing_cost_collector_stddev FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME, SCHOOL_CODE ORDER BY school_clearing_cost_collector_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the average, variance, and standard deviation of the clearing cost collector values for all associated administrative departments, considering only departments that are degree granting and are not the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(a.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS avg_clearing_cost_collector, VARIANCE(a.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS clearing_cost_collector_variance, STDDEV(a.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS clearing_cost_collector_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT a ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Mathematics' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE != '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY clearing_cost_collector_variance DESC;

question: For each school, provide the school name and, for each department in that school that is degree-granting and not 'Political Science', display the average, range, and variance of the department budget codes, along with the count of unique subject codes offered by that department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_CODE, AVG(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_dept_budget_code, MAX(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS range_dept_budget_code, VARIANCE(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS var_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' AND DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT ic.SCHOOL_NAME, ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.avg_dept_budget_code, ic.range_dept_budget_code, ic.var_dept_budget_code, COUNT(DISTINCT ssc.SUBJECT_CODE) AS subject_code_count FROM inner_cte ic LEFT JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ssc.DEPARTMENT_CODE GROUP BY ic.SCHOOL_NAME, ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.avg_dept_budget_code, ic.range_dept_budget_code, ic.var_dept_budget_code ORDER BY ic.SCHOOL_NAME, ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE
sub_questions: For each school, provide the school name and calculate the average, range, and variance of the department budget codes for departments in that school, but only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the 'Political Science' department.
sub_sqls: SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_dept_budget_code, MAX(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS range_dept_budget_code, VARIANCE(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS var_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' AND DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME

question: For each department, what is the highest number of times any course has been offered, and for that course, provide the course number from SIS_SUBJECT_CODE, the course description from SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION, and the subject title from CIS_COURSE_CATALOG? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ssc.COURSE_NUMBER, scd.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, ccc.SUBJECT_TITLE, scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(*) AS offer_count FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON scd.COURSE = ssc.SUBJECT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON ssc.SUBJECT_CODE = ccc.SUBJECT_CODE GROUP BY ssc.COURSE_NUMBER, scd.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, ccc.SUBJECT_TITLE, scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, COURSE_NUMBER, COURSE_DESCRIPTION, SUBJECT_TITLE, MAX(offer_count) AS max_offer_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, COURSE_NUMBER, COURSE_DESCRIPTION, SUBJECT_TITLE;
sub_questions: What are the top 3 most frequently offered courses in the Mathematics department, and for each, provide the course number from SIS_SUBJECT_CODE, the course description from SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION, and the subject title from CIS_COURSE_CATALOG?
sub_sqls: SELECT ssc.COURSE_NUMBER, scd.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, ccc.SUBJECT_TITLE, COUNT(*) AS offer_count FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON scd.COURSE = ssc.SUBJECT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON ssc.SUBJECT_CODE = ccc.SUBJECT_CODE WHERE scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ssc.COURSE_NUMBER, scd.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, ccc.SUBJECT_TITLE ORDER BY offer_count DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each building access level and campus sector, what is the access level name, campus sector, and the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of rooms in building history records for academic buildings, and only for access level and campus sector combinations with more than 5 records? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE, fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_NAME, STDDEV(fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS) AS stddev_num_of_rooms FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE = fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE WHERE fbh.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' GROUP BY fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE, fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ) SELECT fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE, fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_NAME, fbh.CAMPUS_SECTOR, STDDEV(fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS) AS stddev_num_of_rooms FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE = fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE WHERE fbh.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' GROUP BY fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE, fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_NAME, fbh.CAMPUS_SECTOR HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE, fbh.CAMPUS_SECTOR;
sub_questions: For each building access level, what is the access level name and the standard deviation of the number of rooms in building history records for academic buildings, and only for access levels with more than 5 records?
sub_sqls: SELECT fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE, fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_NAME, STDDEV(fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS) AS stddev_num_of_rooms FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE = fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE WHERE fbh.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' GROUP BY fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE, fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ;

question: For each academic year, give the academic year description and find the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered in regular terms by the Mathematics department, but only include those academic years where the average total units for Mathematics subjects is greater than the overall average total units for all subjects offered in regular terms. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, AVG(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE = COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE ACADEMIC_TERMS.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ) SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, avg_total_units, stddev_total_units FROM inner_cte WHERE avg_total_units > ( SELECT AVG(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE = COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE ACADEMIC_TERMS.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' ) ORDER BY stddev_total_units DESC;
sub_questions: For each academic year, give the academic year description and find the average and standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered in terms that are regular terms and are offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, AVG(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE = COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE ACADEMIC_TERMS.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ORDER BY stddev_total_units DESC;

question: For each school, what are the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered in the current academic term, specifically for the Political Science department (Course 17)? Additionally, for each academic year, show these statistics per school, and include a grand total for each school across all academic years in the format of (school name, null, statistics). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ss.SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER atp JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON atp.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE WHERE atp.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' AND ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' GROUP BY ss.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY total_units_variance DESC ), SchoolYearStats AS ( SELECT ss.SCHOOL_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER atp JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON atp.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE WHERE atp.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' AND ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' GROUP BY ss.SCHOOL_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) SELECT sys.SCHOOL_NAME, sys.ACADEMIC_YEAR, sys.avg_total_units, sys.total_units_variance, sys.total_units_stddev FROM SchoolYearStats sys UNION ALL SELECT sys.SCHOOL_NAME, NULL AS ACADEMIC_YEAR, AVG(sys.avg_total_units) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(sys.avg_total_units) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(sys.avg_total_units) AS total_units_stddev FROM SchoolYearStats sys GROUP BY sys.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY SCHOOL_NAME, ACADEMIC_YEAR ;
sub_questions: For each school, what are the average, variance, and standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered in the current academic term, specifically for the Political Science department (Course 17)? Please show the school name along with these statistics.
sub_sqls: SELECT ss.SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER atp JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON atp.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE WHERE atp.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' AND ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' GROUP BY ss.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY total_units_variance DESC;

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding Biology), what is the department name, the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of students in each student year, and the total number of unique courses offered by that department? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, msd.STUDENT_YEAR, COUNT(*) AS num_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Biology' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, msd.STUDENT_YEAR ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(ic.num_students) AS variance_num_students, STDDEV(ic.num_students) AS stddev_num_students, COUNT(DISTINCT ssc.COURSE_NUMBER) AS total_courses FROM inner_cte ic LEFT JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME = d.DEPARTMENT_NAME LEFT JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ssc.DEPARTMENT_CODE GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name and both the variance and standard deviation of the number of students in each student year for that department, considering only departments that are degree granting and are not the Biology department?
sub_sqls: WITH student_counts AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, msd.STUDENT_YEAR, COUNT(*) AS num_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Biology' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, msd.STUDENT_YEAR ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(num_students) AS variance_num_students, STDDEV(num_students) AS stddev_num_students FROM student_counts GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For each department, show the department name, department code, school name, administrative department name, and the average department budget code within each school, as well as the total number of departments per school, for departments that are degree granting, have a non-null department budget code, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.SCHOOL_NAME, a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) OVER (PARTITION BY d.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS avg_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT a ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_CODE, inner_cte.SCHOOL_NAME, inner_cte.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.avg_dept_budget_code, school_counts.total_departments FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(*) AS total_departments FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME ) AS school_counts ON inner_cte.SCHOOL_NAME = school_counts.SCHOOL_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, show the department name, department code, school name, administrative department name, and the average department budget code within each school, ordered by department code, for departments that are degree granting, have a non-null department budget code, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.SCHOOL_NAME, a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) OVER (PARTITION BY d.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS avg_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT a ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each school, show the school name, the number of degree-granting departments in the school that have a non-null department budget code and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18), and the average of their average department budget codes (partitioned by school), ordered by school name. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.SCHOOL_NAME, a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) OVER (PARTITION BY d.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS avg_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT a ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS num_departments, AVG(avg_dept_budget_code) AS avg_of_avg_budget_code FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY SCHOOL_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, show the department name, department code, school name, administrative department name, and the average department budget code within each school, ordered by department code, for departments that are degree granting, have a non-null department budget code, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.SCHOOL_NAME, a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) OVER (PARTITION BY d.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS avg_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT a ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each school and department, what is the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of CIP program codes among all courses offered by departments in that school, restricted to degree-granting courses in the Mathematics department (Course 18)? Also, include the department's full name and phone number in the results. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.SCHOOL_NAME, SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE, VARIANCE(SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_program_code_variance, STDDEV(SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_program_code_stddev FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT ON SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT = SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = SIS_SUBJECT_CODE.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.SCHOOL_NAME, SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT inner_cte.SCHOOL_NAME, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, inner_cte.cip_program_code_variance, inner_cte.cip_program_code_stddev FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE LEFT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ad ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY inner_cte.cip_program_code_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each school, what is the variance and standard deviation of CIP program codes among all courses offered by departments in that school, restricted to the Mathematics department (Course 18) and only for degree-granting courses?
sub_sqls: SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.SCHOOL_NAME, VARIANCE(SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_program_code_variance, STDDEV(SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_program_code_stddev FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT ON SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT = SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = SIS_SUBJECT_CODE.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY cip_program_code_variance DESC;

question: List the subject titles, their corresponding department names, and the variance of the record count for tip details associated with each subject, considering only subjects offered by the "Harvard Cross-Enrollment Prog" department, with a total number of units greater than 0, and excluding subjects from the Chemistry department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ss.SUBJECT_TITLE, VARIANCE(td.RECORD_COUNT) AS record_count_variance FROM TIP_DETAIL td JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED so ON td.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON so.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE WHERE so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Harvard Cross-Enrollment Prog' AND ss.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME != 'Chemistry' GROUP BY ss.SUBJECT_TITLE ) SELECT inner_cte.SUBJECT_TITLE, ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.record_count_variance FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON inner_cte.SUBJECT_TITLE = ss.SUBJECT_TITLE ORDER BY inner_cte.record_count_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each subject title, what is the variance of the record count for tip details associated with that subject, considering only subjects offered by the "Harvard Cross-Enrollment Prog" department, with a total number of units greater than 0, and excluding subjects from the Chemistry department?
sub_sqls: SELECT ss.SUBJECT_TITLE, VARIANCE(td.RECORD_COUNT) AS record_count_variance FROM TIP_DETAIL td JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED so ON td.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON so.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE WHERE so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Harvard Cross-Enrollment Prog' AND ss.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME != 'Chemistry' GROUP BY ss.SUBJECT_TITLE ORDER BY record_count_variance DESC;

question: For each department name and course level where the department is degree granting and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique courses, the minimum CIP program code, and the number of unique subject codes associated with those courses. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.COURSE_LEVEL, COUNT(DISTINCT c.COURSE) AS course_count, MIN(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS min_cip_code FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.COURSE_LEVEL ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.COURSE_LEVEL, ic.course_count, ic.min_cip_code, COUNT(DISTINCT s.SUBJECT_CODE) AS subject_code_count FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME = d.DEPARTMENT_NAME JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.COURSE_LEVEL, ic.course_count, ic.min_cip_code;
sub_questions: For each department name and course level where the department is degree granting and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique courses and the minimum CIP program code.
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.COURSE_LEVEL, COUNT(DISTINCT c.COURSE) AS course_count, MIN(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS min_cip_code FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.COURSE_LEVEL;

question: For each school, what are the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that school, considering only subjects with more than 0 enrolled students and courses that are degree granting, and only for the School of Science? Additionally, for each school, include a grand total for all departments in the format of (school, null, total units statistics). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON scd.COURSE = sos.COURSE_NUMBER WHERE scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND scd.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Science' GROUP BY scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME, avg_total_units, total_units_variance, total_units_stddev FROM ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME, avg_total_units, total_units_variance, total_units_stddev FROM inner_cte UNION ALL SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, NULL AS DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(avg_total_units) AS avg_total_units, AVG(total_units_variance) AS total_units_variance, AVG(total_units_stddev) AS total_units_stddev FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME ) t ORDER BY SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME
sub_questions: For each department, what are the average, variance, and standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, considering only subjects with more than 0 enrolled students and courses that are degree granting, and only for the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON scd.COURSE = sos.COURSE_NUMBER WHERE scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND scd.DEPARTMENT = '18' GROUP BY scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY total_units_variance DESC;

question: For each Mathematics department subject, list the subject ID, the minimum number of enrolled students, the average lecture units, and the total number of terms offered for each subject, for subjects where the number of enrolled students is between 2 and 10 or the academic year is at least 2020, and the term start date is between '01-JAN-20' and '31-DEC-22'. Additionally, for each subject, include a grand total row showing the overall minimum number of enrolled students, average lecture units, and total terms across all subjects. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT c.SUBJECT_ID, MIN(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS min_num_enrolled_students, AVG(c.LECTURE_UNITS) AS avg_lecture_units, COUNT(DISTINCT c.TERM_CODE) AS total_terms FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL a ON c.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t ON t.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE AND t.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID WHERE c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ( (t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS BETWEEN 2 AND 10) OR (a.ACADEMIC_YEAR >= 2020) ) AND a.TERM_START_DATE BETWEEN '01-JAN-20' AND '31-DEC-22' GROUP BY c.SUBJECT_ID ) SELECT SUBJECT_ID, min_num_enrolled_students, avg_lecture_units, total_terms FROM inner_cte UNION ALL SELECT NULL AS SUBJECT_ID, MIN(min_num_enrolled_students) AS min_num_enrolled_students, AVG(avg_lecture_units) AS avg_lecture_units, SUM(total_terms) AS total_terms FROM inner_cte ORDER BY SUBJECT_ID
sub_questions: For each subject, give the subject ID, the minimum number of enrolled students and the average lecture units for each subject in the Mathematics department, for subjects where the number of enrolled students is between 2 and 10 or the academic year is at least 2020, and the term start date is between '01-JAN-20' and '31-DEC-22'.
sub_sqls: SELECT c.SUBJECT_ID, MIN(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS min_num_enrolled_students, AVG(c.LECTURE_UNITS) AS avg_lecture_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL a ON c.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t ON t.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE AND t.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID WHERE c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ( (t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS BETWEEN 2 AND 10) OR (a.ACADEMIC_YEAR >= 2020) ) AND a.TERM_START_DATE BETWEEN '01-JAN-20' AND '31-DEC-22' GROUP BY c.SUBJECT_ID;

question: For each term description in the academic year 2024, show the term description and the highest rank achieved by any Mathematics subject (ordered by subject code) within that term. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION ORDER BY t0.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) SELECT TERM_DESCRIPTION, MAX(window_column) AS highest_rank FROM inner_cte GROUP BY TERM_DESCRIPTION;
sub_questions: For all subjects offered in the academic year 2024 by the Mathematics department, show the subject code, subject title, term description, and the rank of each subject within its term description group ordered by subject code.
sub_sqls: SELECT t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION ORDER BY t0.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each academic year and school, what is the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units offered per academic term in that year for the Mathematics department (Course 18), along with the school name? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, at.TERM_CODE, SUM(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_per_term, ss.SCHOOL_NAME FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS at JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE WHERE ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, at.TERM_CODE, ss.SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, SCHOOL_NAME, MAX(total_units_per_term) - MIN(total_units_per_term) AS units_range, VARIANCE(total_units_per_term) AS units_variance, STDDEV(total_units_per_term) AS units_stddev FROM inner_cte GROUP BY ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, SCHOOL_NAME;
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the range, variance, and standard deviation of the total units offered per academic term in that year for the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: WITH term_units AS ( SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, at.TERM_CODE, SUM(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_per_term FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS at JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE WHERE ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, at.TERM_CODE ) SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, MAX(total_units_per_term) - MIN(total_units_per_term) AS units_range, VARIANCE(total_units_per_term) AS units_variance, STDDEV(total_units_per_term) AS units_stddev FROM term_units GROUP BY ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ORDER BY ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ;

question: For students whose department is degree-granting, whose student year is 'G', and who are in the Political Science department, show their full name, email address, department full name, and whether their email address contains 'mit.edu' (label as 'MIT_EMAIL') or not (label as 'NON_MIT_EMAIL'). Only include students whose first name is 'Zoe'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t1.FULL_NAME, t1.EMAIL_ADDRESS, t0.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT WHERE t0.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND t1.FIRST_NAME = 'Zoe' AND t1.DEPARTMENT = '17' ) SELECT inner_cte.FULL_NAME, inner_cte.EMAIL_ADDRESS, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, CASE WHEN inner_cte.EMAIL_ADDRESS LIKE '%mit.edu%' THEN 'MIT_EMAIL' ELSE 'NON_MIT_EMAIL' END AS email_type FROM inner_cte;
sub_questions: For students whose department is degree-granting, whose student year is 'G', and who are in the Political Science department, show their full name, email address, department full name, and assign row numbers within a window of 2 preceding and 1 following rows ordered by the student's full name. Additionally, only include students whose first name is 'Zoe'.
sub_sqls: SELECT t1.FULL_NAME, t1.EMAIL_ADDRESS, t0.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY t1.FULL_NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT WHERE t0.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND t1.FIRST_NAME = 'Zoe' AND t1.DEPARTMENT = '17'

question: For each academic year, what is the academic year description, and for each Mathematics (Course 18) subject offered in that year, what is the subject id, subject title, total units, and the deviation of its total units from the average total units of Mathematics subjects in that year, considering only years with more than 5 Mathematics subjects? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.SUBJECT_ID, COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.SUBJECT_TITLE, COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS ON SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE = COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) , avg_units_per_year AS ( SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR, AVG(TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, COUNT(*) AS subject_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY ACADEMIC_YEAR HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ) SELECT i.ACADEMIC_YEAR, i.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, i.SUBJECT_ID, i.SUBJECT_TITLE, i.TOTAL_UNITS, (i.TOTAL_UNITS - a.avg_total_units) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN avg_units_per_year a ON i.ACADEMIC_YEAR = a.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY i.ACADEMIC_YEAR DESC, deviation_from_avg DESC;
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the academic year description and the standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered in terms within that year, considering only years with more than 5 subjects, and only including subjects from the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, STDDEV(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS ON SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE = COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY total_units_stddev DESC;

question: For each school, what is the geometric mean of the department budget codes for degree-granting departments in that school, excluding the Political Science department (Course 17), and what is the count of unique subject codes associated with those departments? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_CODE, EXP(AVG(LOG(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE))) AS geometric_mean_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' AND DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT ic.SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(ic.geometric_mean_dept_budget_code) AS school_geometric_mean_dept_budget_code, COUNT(DISTINCT ssc.SUBJECT_CODE) AS unique_subject_code_count FROM inner_cte ic LEFT JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ssc.DEPARTMENT_CODE GROUP BY ic.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY ic.SCHOOL_NAME;
sub_questions: For each school, what is the geometric mean of the department budget codes for degree-granting departments in that school, excluding the Political Science department (Course 17)?
sub_sqls: SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, EXP(AVG(LOG(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE))) AS geometric_mean_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' AND DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY SCHOOL_NAME;

question: For each degree-granting department whose code is '18' (Mathematics), and for subjects offered by that department in the term 2019FA, what is the department name, the variance of the number of enrolled students in those subjects, and the number of subjects offered, restricted to departments that offered at least 5 subjects in that term? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS variance_num_enrolled_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.variance_num_enrolled_students, COUNT(tso.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_subjects_offered FROM inner_cte JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.variance_num_enrolled_students HAVING COUNT(tso.SUBJECT_ID) >= 5;
sub_questions: For each department that grants degrees, what is the department name and the variance of the number of enrolled students in subjects offered by that department in the term 2019FA, restricted to departments whose department code is '18' (Mathematics)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS variance_num_enrolled_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For each department that grants degrees, what is the department's full name, the range and variance of the number of enrolled students in subjects offered by that department (considering only subjects with more than 0 enrolled students), and whether the department is a 'HIGH_VARIANCE' department (variance at least 50), 'LOW_VARIANCE' (variance less than 10), or 'MEDIUM_VARIANCE' otherwise? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, MAX(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) - MIN(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_students_range, VARIANCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_students_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, inner_cte.enrolled_students_range, inner_cte.enrolled_students_variance, CASE WHEN inner_cte.enrolled_students_variance >= 50 THEN 'HIGH_VARIANCE' WHEN inner_cte.enrolled_students_variance < 10 THEN 'LOW_VARIANCE' ELSE 'MEDIUM_VARIANCE' END AS variance_category FROM inner_cte;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department's full name, and what are the range and variance of the number of enrolled students in subjects offered by that department, considering only subjects with more than 0 enrolled students and departments that grant degrees, but only for the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, MAX(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) - MIN(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_students_range, VARIANCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_students_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME;

question: For each room in the Stata building with area greater than 50 and access level equal to 1, excluding rooms assigned to the department of facilities, show the room key, area, organization name, building name, and the dense rank of each room within its building, and also include the building's total assignable area. Order the results by building key and room key. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, fr.AREA, fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME, fb.BUILDING_NAME, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY) AS room_dense_rank, fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY FROM FCLT_ROOMS fr JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = '32' AND fr.AREA > 50 AND fr.ACCESS_LEVEL = 1 AND fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME <> 'DP OF FACILITIES' ) SELECT ic.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, ic.AREA, ic.ORGANIZATION_NAME, ic.BUILDING_NAME, ic.room_dense_rank, fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA FROM inner_cte ic JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON ic.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY ic.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, ic.FCLT_ROOM_KEY;
domain_knowledge: "department of facilities" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_NAME = 'DP OF FACILITIES'"
sub_questions: Show the room key, area, and organization name for each room in the Stata building, along with the building name and the dense rank of each room within its building, ordered by building key, for rooms with area greater than 50 and access level equal to 1, excluding rooms assigned to the department of facilities.
sub_sqls: SELECT fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, fr.AREA, fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME, fb.BUILDING_NAME, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY) AS room_dense_rank FROM FCLT_ROOMS fr JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = '32' AND fr.AREA > 50 AND fr.ACCESS_LEVEL = 1 AND fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME <> 'DP OF FACILITIES' ORDER BY fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY;

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding the Mathematics department), provide the department name, the average and variance of the ASCII values of its subject codes' course numbers, but only include those departments where the average ASCII value is greater than the overall average ASCII value across all degree-granting departments (excluding Mathematics). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(ASCII(s.COURSE_NUMBER)) AS avg_course_number_ascii, VARIANCE(ASCII(s.COURSE_NUMBER)) AS var_course_number_ascii FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Mathematics' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, avg_course_number_ascii, var_course_number_ascii FROM inner_cte WHERE avg_course_number_ascii > ( SELECT AVG(avg_course_number_ascii) FROM inner_cte ) ORDER BY var_course_number_ascii DESC;
