sub_questions: What is the minimum organization level and the total number of assignable organizations for organizations that belong to departments under the 'Provost Area' in the department hierarchy, excluding organizations '138' and '250', and only including organizations that are assignable?
sub_sqls: SELECT MIN(f.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) AS min_org_level, SUM(f.ASSIGNABLE) AS total_assignable FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY m JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT h ON m.DLC_KEY = h.DLC_KEY JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION f ON h.DLC_KEY = f.DLC_KEY WHERE m.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_NAME = 'Provost Area' AND f.ASSIGNABLE = 1 AND f.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250')

question: For each school, provide the school name and, for each department in that school that is degree-granting and not 'Political Science', list the department name, and calculate the average, range, and variance of the subject codes' lengths for subjects offered by that department. For each school, also include a grand total for all departments in the format of (school name, null, averages for all departments). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' AND DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL ) , SubjectStats AS ( SELECT ic.SCHOOL_NAME, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, LENGTH(sc.SUBJECT_CODE) AS subject_code_length FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE sc ON ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sc.SUBJECT_CODE IS NOT NULL ) SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(subject_code_length) AS avg_subject_code_length, MAX(subject_code_length) - MIN(subject_code_length) AS range_subject_code_length, VARIANCE(subject_code_length) AS var_subject_code_length FROM SubjectStats GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME WITH ROLLUP HAVING SCHOOL_NAME IS NOT NULL ORDER BY SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME
sub_questions: For each school, provide the school name and calculate the average, range, and variance of the department budget codes for departments in that school, but only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the 'Political Science' department.
sub_sqls: SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_dept_budget_code, MAX(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS range_dept_budget_code, VARIANCE(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS var_dept_budget_code FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' AND DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME

question: For each course offered by a degree-granting department in the School of Engineering, except for the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science department, in the 2007 academic year, show the course key, course name, department name, the number of catalog subjects, the total units for those subjects, and the graduate level of the course. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT scd.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY, scd.COURSE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(ccc.SUBJECT_ID) AS subject_count, SUM(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON scd.DEPARTMENT = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND ccc.ACADEMIC_YEAR = '2007' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' GROUP BY scd.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY, scd.COURSE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY, inner_cte.COURSE, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.subject_count, inner_cte.total_units, scd.GRADUATE_LEVEL FROM inner_cte JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON inner_cte.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY = scd.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY;
domain_knowledge: "Computer Science" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
"except Cambridge-MIT Institute" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_NAME NOT IN ('CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST')"
"Electrical Engineering and Computer Science" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
sub_questions: For each course offered by a degree-granting department in the School of Engineering, except for the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science department, what is the course key, course name, department name, and the number of catalog subjects and the total units for those subjects in the 2007 academic year?
sub_sqls: SELECT scd.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY, scd.COURSE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(ccc.SUBJECT_ID) AS subject_count, SUM(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON scd.DEPARTMENT = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND ccc.ACADEMIC_YEAR = '2007' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' GROUP BY scd.SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION_KEY, scd.COURSE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For each building in the city of CAMBRIDGE that is used as a residence, what is the maximum assignable area among its floors, what is the building's name, and what is the total number of rooms in the building? Exclude the Stata building from the results, and only include buildings where the maximum assignable area among its floors is greater than the average assignable area of all floors in CAMBRIDGE residential buildings (excluding the Stata building). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fb.BUILDING_NAME, MAX(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS MAX_ASSIGNABLE_AREA, fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fba.CITY = 'CAMBRIDGE' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND fb.BUILDING_NAME <> 'Ray and Maria Stata Center' GROUP BY fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS ) SELECT BUILDING_NAME, MAX_ASSIGNABLE_AREA, NUM_OF_ROOMS FROM inner_cte WHERE MAX_ASSIGNABLE_AREA > ( SELECT AVG(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fba.CITY = 'CAMBRIDGE' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND fb.BUILDING_NAME <> 'Ray and Maria Stata Center' ) ;
domain_knowledge: "used as a residence" is predicated by "TABLE.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT'"
"Stata building" is predicated by "TABLE.BUILDING_NAME = 'Ray and Maria Stata Center'"
sub_questions: For each building in the city of CAMBRIDGE that is used as a residence, what is the maximum assignable area among its floors, and what is the building's name? Exclude the Stata building from the results.
sub_sqls: SELECT fb.BUILDING_NAME, MAX(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS MAX_ASSIGNABLE_AREA FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fba.CITY = 'CAMBRIDGE' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND fb.BUILDING_NAME <> 'Ray and Maria Stata Center' GROUP BY fb.BUILDING_NAME

question: For academic buildings where the total number of rooms is greater than the average number of rooms across all academic buildings, list the building name and the total number of rooms, showing only the top 10 such buildings. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.BUILDING_NAME, COUNT(r.FCLT_ROOM_KEY) AS room_count FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST b JOIN FCLT_ROOMS r ON b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = r.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE b.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' GROUP BY b.BUILDING_NAME ) SELECT BUILDING_NAME, room_count FROM inner_cte WHERE room_count > ( SELECT AVG(room_count) FROM inner_cte ) ORDER BY room_count DESC LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: List the top 10 academic building names by the number of rooms they contain, along with the total number of rooms for each building.
sub_sqls: SELECT b.BUILDING_NAME, COUNT(r.FCLT_ROOM_KEY) AS room_count FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST b JOIN FCLT_ROOMS r ON b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = r.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE b.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' GROUP BY b.BUILDING_NAME ORDER BY room_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each school, provide the school name and the highest average total units for degree-granting courses offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18), grouped by course level (undergraduate or graduate), considering only courses with a non-null total units value. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT scd.SCHOOL_NAME, scd.COURSE_LEVEL, ccc.TOTAL_UNITS FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON scd.COURSE = ssc.SUBJECT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON ssc.SUBJECT_CODE = ccc.SUBJECT_CODE WHERE scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccc.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL AND scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, MAX(avg_total_units) AS highest_avg_total_units FROM ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, COURSE_LEVEL, AVG(TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME, COURSE_LEVEL ) subquery1 GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY highest_avg_total_units DESC;
sub_questions: For each school, provide the school name and calculate the average, range, and variance of the total units for courses offered by that school, considering only courses that are degree granting, have a non-null total units value, and are offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT scd.SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, MAX(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_range, VARIANCE(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON scd.COURSE = ssc.SUBJECT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON ssc.SUBJECT_CODE = ccc.SUBJECT_CODE WHERE scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccc.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL AND scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY scd.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY total_units_range DESC;

question: For each school, what is the school name and both the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of students in each student year for each department in that school, considering only departments that are degree granting and are not the Biology department? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH student_counts AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, msd.STUDENT_YEAR, COUNT(*) AS num_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Biology' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, msd.STUDENT_YEAR ) SELECT d.SCHOOL_NAME, sc.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sc.STUDENT_YEAR, sc.num_students FROM student_counts sc JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON sc.DEPARTMENT_NAME = d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, VARIANCE(num_students) AS variance_num_students, STDDEV(num_students) AS stddev_num_students FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name and both the variance and standard deviation of the number of students in each student year for that department, considering only departments that are degree granting and are not the Biology department?
sub_sqls: WITH student_counts AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, msd.STUDENT_YEAR, COUNT(*) AS num_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Biology' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, msd.STUDENT_YEAR ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(num_students) AS variance_num_students, STDDEV(num_students) AS stddev_num_students FROM student_counts GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For each administrative department, give the administrative department name and the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the academic year 2024, but only include departments whose name is 'Mechanical Engineering' (Course 2) and where the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) is greater than 0.2. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE UPPER(sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) = 'MECHANICAL ENGINEERING' AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 GROUP BY sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte WHERE coefficient_of_variation > 0.2;
sub_questions: For each administrative department, give the administrative department name and the coefficient of variation of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the academic year 2024, but only include departments whose name is 'Mechanical Engineering' (Course 2).
sub_sqls: SELECT sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE UPPER(sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) = 'MECHANICAL ENGINEERING' AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 GROUP BY sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: For each department, give the department name and the highest coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department across all terms, but only include departments that are not 'Biology' (Course 7). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department_name, (STDDEV_SAMP(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS), 0)) AS coefficient_of_variation, sos.TERM_CODE FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED so ON sos.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON so.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID WHERE sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME <> 'Biology' GROUP BY sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, sos.TERM_CODE HAVING COUNT(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ) SELECT department_name, MAX(coefficient_of_variation) AS highest_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte GROUP BY department_name;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the coefficient of variation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, but only include departments that are not 'Biology' (Course 7).
sub_sqls: SELECT sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department_name, (STDDEV_SAMP(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS), 0)) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED so ON sos.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON so.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID WHERE sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME <> 'Biology' GROUP BY sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ;

question: List the top 10 subject titles offered by the Chemistry department along with their department names, the number of course materials assigned to each, and the total number of enrolled students for each subject, for subjects that have at least one enrolled student and at least one course material record. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS num_course_materials FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON tso.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID WHERE tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Chemistry' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 GROUP BY tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME HAVING num_course_materials > 0 ) SELECT icte.SUBJECT_TITLE, icte.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, icte.num_course_materials, SUM(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrolled_students FROM inner_cte icte JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON icte.SUBJECT_TITLE = tso.SUBJECT_TITLE AND icte.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME GROUP BY icte.SUBJECT_TITLE, icte.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, icte.num_course_materials ORDER BY icte.num_course_materials DESC, icte.SUBJECT_TITLE LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: List the top 10 subject titles offered by the Chemistry department along with their department names and the number of course materials assigned to each, for subjects that have at least one enrolled student and at least one course material record.
sub_sqls: SELECT tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS num_course_materials FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON tso.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID WHERE tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Chemistry' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 GROUP BY tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME HAVING num_course_materials > 0 ORDER BY num_course_materials DESC, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE LIMIT 10;

question: For each department, provide the department name, the total number of enrolled students in subjects offered by degree-granting departments (excluding Chemistry), and the average number of enrolled students per subject for those departments that have at least 100 total enrolled students. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, SUM(sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrolled_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE HAVING SUM(sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) >= 100 ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.total_enrolled_students, AVG(sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrolled_per_subject FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE GROUP BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.total_enrolled_students ORDER BY inner_cte.total_enrolled_students DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and calculate the total number of enrolled students in subjects offered by departments that are degree granting, have at least 100 total enrolled students, and are not the Chemistry department (Course 5).
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrolled_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING SUM(sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) >= 100 ORDER BY total_enrolled_students DESC;

question: For each academic year and each department, what is the average and variance of the total units for subjects offered, considering only subjects that are offered in the fall term, are not variable units, and are in departments whose names contain 'Mathematics'? For each academic year, include a grand total for all such departments in the format of (academic year, null, total statistics). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR, cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, cso.TOTAL_UNITS FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso WHERE cso.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND cso.IS_VARIABLE_UNITS = 'N' AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME LIKE '%Mathematics%' ) SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR, DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(TOTAL_UNITS) AS var_total_units FROM inner_cte GROUP BY ACADEMIC_YEAR, DEPARTMENT_NAME WITH ROLLUP HAVING ACADEMIC_YEAR IS NOT NULL ORDER BY ACADEMIC_YEAR, DEPARTMENT_NAME
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the average and variance of the total units for subjects offered, considering only subjects that are offered in the fall term, are not variable units, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18)? Show the academic year and these statistics.
sub_sqls: SELECT cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR, AVG(cso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(cso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS var_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso WHERE cso.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND cso.IS_VARIABLE_UNITS = 'N' AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR

question: For rooms with an area greater than 100 and an access level of 1, in the Stata building, show the building room identifier, the room's area, the organization name, and the building number, and assign row numbers within a window of 2 preceding and 1 following rows ordered by the building number from the building address, excluding rooms belonging to the department of facilities. Only include results where the building number ends with '2' and the total number of such rooms per organization is at least 3. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fr.BUILDING_ROOM, fr.AREA, fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY fba.BUILDING_NUMBER ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS row_num_window, fba.BUILDING_NUMBER FROM FCLT_ROOMS fr JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba ON fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fr.AREA > 100 AND fr.ACCESS_LEVEL = 1 AND fba.BUILDING_NUMBER = '32' AND fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME <> 'DP OF FACILITIES' ) SELECT ic.BUILDING_ROOM, ic.AREA, ic.ORGANIZATION_NAME, ic.BUILDING_NUMBER, ic.row_num_window FROM inner_cte ic JOIN ( SELECT ORGANIZATION_NAME FROM inner_cte WHERE BUILDING_NUMBER LIKE '%2' GROUP BY ORGANIZATION_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ) orgs ON ic.ORGANIZATION_NAME = orgs.ORGANIZATION_NAME WHERE ic.BUILDING_NUMBER LIKE '%2'
domain_knowledge: "department of facilities" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_NAME = 'DP OF FACILITIES'"
sub_questions: For rooms with an area greater than 100 and an access level of 1, in the Stata building, show the building room identifier, the room's area, the organization name, and assign row numbers within a window of 2 preceding and 1 following rows ordered by the building number from the building address, excluding rooms belonging to the department of facilities.
sub_sqls: SELECT fr.BUILDING_ROOM, fr.AREA, fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY fba.BUILDING_NUMBER ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS row_num_window FROM FCLT_ROOMS fr JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba ON fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fr.AREA > 100 AND fr.ACCESS_LEVEL = 1 AND fba.BUILDING_NUMBER = '32' AND fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME <> 'DP OF FACILITIES'

question: For each academic year, what is the academic year description, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for all subjects offered in terms that are marked as the current term in the term parameter table and are offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18), and what is the total number of such Mathematics subjects per academic year? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, STDDEV(sub.TOTAL_UNITS)/NULLIF(AVG(sub.TOTAL_UNITS),0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED sub JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL aca ON sub.TERM_CODE = aca.TERM_CODE JOIN ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER param ON aca.TERM_CODE = param.TERM_CODE WHERE param.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' AND sub.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND sub.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC HAVING AVG(sub.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ) SELECT inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation, subj_count.total_subjects FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(DISTINCT sub.SUBJECT_ID) AS total_subjects FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED sub JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL aca ON sub.TERM_CODE = aca.TERM_CODE JOIN ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER param ON aca.TERM_CODE = param.TERM_CODE WHERE param.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' AND sub.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND sub.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) subj_count ON inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR = subj_count.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation DESC;
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the academic year description and the coefficient of variation of the total units for all subjects offered in terms that are marked as the current term in the term parameter table and are offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, STDDEV(sub.TOTAL_UNITS)/NULLIF(AVG(sub.TOTAL_UNITS),0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED sub JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL aca ON sub.TERM_CODE = aca.TERM_CODE JOIN ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER param ON aca.TERM_CODE = param.TERM_CODE WHERE param.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' AND sub.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND sub.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, aca.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC HAVING AVG(sub.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For each department, give the department name, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department (considering only subjects with more than 0 total units), and the name of the corresponding administrative department (if any), restricting the results to the Mathematics department (Course 18). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) / AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation, sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad ON sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME = inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the coefficient of variation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, considering only departments that have at least one subject with more than 0 total units, and restrict the results to the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) / AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: From the top 5 Mathematics department subjects offered in the 2022 academic year with the highest maximum enrollment (where the maximum enrollment is greater than 10), display each subject's title, the maximum number of enrolled students, the term description in which this maximum occurred, and the name of the instructor most frequently responsible for the subject (along with the count of terms they taught it). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT c.SUBJECT_TITLE, MAX(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS max_enrollment, a.TERM_DESCRIPTION, c.SUBJECT_ID FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS a ON c.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t ON a.TERM_CODE = t.TERM_CODE AND c.SUBJECT_ID = t.SUBJECT_ID WHERE a.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY c.SUBJECT_TITLE, a.TERM_DESCRIPTION, c.SUBJECT_ID HAVING MAX(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) > 10 ) SELECT ic.SUBJECT_TITLE, ic.max_enrollment, ic.TERM_DESCRIPTION, imf.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS Most_Frequent_Instructor, imf.Terms_Taught FROM ( SELECT SUBJECT_TITLE, MAX(max_enrollment) AS max_enrollment, TERM_DESCRIPTION, SUBJECT_ID FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SUBJECT_TITLE, TERM_DESCRIPTION, SUBJECT_ID ) ic LEFT JOIN ( SELECT t.SUBJECT_ID, t.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, COUNT(*) AS Terms_Taught, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.SUBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) as rn FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t WHERE t.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY t.SUBJECT_ID, t.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME ) imf ON ic.SUBJECT_ID = imf.SUBJECT_ID AND imf.rn = 1 ORDER BY ic.max_enrollment DESC LIMIT 5;
sub_questions: For each subject offered in the 2022 academic year by the Mathematics department, what is the maximum number of enrolled students for that subject, and what is the term description in which this maximum occurred, considering only subjects where the maximum enrollment is greater than 10?
sub_sqls: SELECT c.SUBJECT_TITLE, MAX(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS max_enrollment, a.TERM_DESCRIPTION FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS a ON c.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t ON a.TERM_CODE = t.TERM_CODE AND c.SUBJECT_ID = t.SUBJECT_ID WHERE a.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY c.SUBJECT_TITLE, a.TERM_DESCRIPTION HAVING MAX(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) > 10;

question: For each department, list the department name and the highest number of course materials assigned to any subject offered by that department, considering only subjects that have at least one enrolled student and at least one course material record. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS num_course_materials FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON tso.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID WHERE tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 GROUP BY tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME HAVING num_course_materials > 0 ) SELECT OFFER_DEPT_NAME, MAX(num_course_materials) AS highest_num_course_materials FROM inner_cte GROUP BY OFFER_DEPT_NAME;
sub_questions: List the top 10 subject titles offered by the Chemistry department along with their department names and the number of course materials assigned to each, for subjects that have at least one enrolled student and at least one course material record.
sub_sqls: SELECT tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS num_course_materials FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON tso.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID WHERE tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Chemistry' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 GROUP BY tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME HAVING num_course_materials > 0 ORDER BY num_course_materials DESC, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE LIMIT 10;

question: For each department and school, what is the highest number of degree-granting undergraduate courses in the Mathematics department (Course 18), and what are the corresponding department name, school name, and the number of unique subject codes associated with those courses? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(*) AS num_courses FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND COURSE_LEVEL = 'U' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.SCHOOL_NAME, i.num_courses, COUNT(DISTINCT s.SUBJECT_CODE) AS num_subject_codes FROM inner_cte i JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c ON c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = i.DEPARTMENT_NAME AND c.SCHOOL_NAME = i.SCHOOL_NAME JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON s.DEPARTMENT_NAME = c.DEPARTMENT_NAME AND s.SCHOOL_NAME = c.SCHOOL_NAME WHERE c.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND c.COURSE_LEVEL = 'U' AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.SCHOOL_NAME, i.num_courses ORDER BY i.num_courses DESC LIMIT 1;
sub_questions: Which department name and school name have the highest number of courses, considering only courses that are degree granting, have a course level of 'U', and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(*) AS num_courses FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION WHERE IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND COURSE_LEVEL = 'U' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY num_courses DESC LIMIT 1;

question: For each school and department, what is the name of the school, the department name, and the variance of the CIP program code for all courses that are degree granting, have a non-null department name, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18)? Show the results grouped by school and department, and order by the variance in descending order. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.SCHOOL_NAME, VARIANCE(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_code_variance FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c ON s.SUBJECT_CODE = c.COURSE WHERE c.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME IS NOT NULL AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY s.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY cip_code_variance DESC ) SELECT ic.SCHOOL_NAME, sc.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.cip_code_variance FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE sc ON ic.SCHOOL_NAME = sc.SCHOOL_NAME GROUP BY ic.SCHOOL_NAME, sc.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.cip_code_variance ORDER BY ic.cip_code_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each school, what is the name of the school and the variance of the CIP program code for all courses that are degree granting, have a non-null department name, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT s.SCHOOL_NAME, VARIANCE(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_code_variance FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c ON s.SUBJECT_CODE = c.COURSE WHERE c.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME IS NOT NULL AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY s.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY cip_code_variance DESC;

question: For each building, list the floor number, the number of rooms on that floor with an area greater than 500 and whose major use description does not include 'STORAGE', and the total area of such rooms. For each building, include a grand total for all floors in the format of (building key, null, total rooms, total area). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, ff.FLOOR, fr.AREA, fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC FROM FCLT_ROOMS fr JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AND fr.FLOOR = ff.FLOOR WHERE fr.AREA > 500 AND (fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC IS NULL OR fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC NOT LIKE '%STORAGE%') ) SELECT FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, FLOOR, COUNT(FCLT_ROOM_KEY) AS num_rooms, SUM(AREA) AS total_area FROM inner_cte GROUP BY FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, FLOOR WITH ROLLUP HAVING COUNT(FCLT_ROOM_KEY) > 0 ORDER BY FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, FLOOR
domain_knowledge: "exclude usage types that include 'STORAGE'" is predicated by "TABLE.SPACE_USAGE NOT LIKE '%STORAGE%'"
sub_questions: For rooms with an area greater than 500 in the Stata building, excluding rooms whose major use description includes 'STORAGE', show the room key, building key, floor number, major use description, and the rank of each room within its building ordered by room key.
sub_sqls: SELECT fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, ff.FLOOR, fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY) AS room_rank_in_building FROM FCLT_ROOMS fr JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AND fr.FLOOR = ff.FLOOR WHERE fr.AREA > 500 AND fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = '32' AND (fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC IS NULL OR fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC NOT LIKE '%STORAGE%') ORDER BY fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, room_rank_in_building;

question: Among all degree-granting departments except Chemistry (Course 5), which department had the highest average total units for subjects offered in the 2008 academic year, and what is the range and variance of total units for subjects in that department? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, MAX(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_range, VARIANCE(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, AVG(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccc.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2008 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.avg_total_units, ic.total_units_range, ic.total_units_variance FROM inner_cte ic WHERE ic.avg_total_units = ( SELECT MAX(avg_total_units) FROM inner_cte )
sub_questions: For each department, provide the department's name and calculate the range and variance of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the 2008 academic year, but only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the Chemistry department (Course 5).
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_range, VARIANCE(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccc.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2008 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME

question: For each academic year, what is the range and variance of the total units for subjects offered in terms that start after January 1, 2010 and are regular terms, specifically for subjects in the Mathematics department, and what is the total number of such Mathematics subjects offered per academic year? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, MAX(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_range, VARIANCE(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND at.TERM_START_DATE > '2010-01-01' AND at.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) SELECT inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, inner_cte.total_units_range, inner_cte.total_units_variance, subject_counts.total_subjects FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(DISTINCT ccso.SUBJECT_ID) AS total_subjects FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND at.TERM_START_DATE > '2010-01-01' AND at.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) AS subject_counts ON inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR = subject_counts.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR;
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the range and variance of the total units for subjects offered in terms that start after January 1, 2010 and are regular terms, specifically for subjects in the Mathematics department?
sub_sqls: SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, MAX(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_range, VARIANCE(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND at.TERM_START_DATE > '2010-01-01' AND at.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR;

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding Chemistry) that offered at least one subject in the term '2016SP', display the department name, the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of subjects offered per term by that department, as well as the term in which the department offered the most subjects and the corresponding number of subjects in that term. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH dept_terms AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING, sos.TERM_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.TERM_CODE = '2016SP' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Chemistry' ), subjects_per_term AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sos.TERM_CODE, COUNT(sos.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_subjects FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Chemistry' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sos.TERM_CODE ) SELECT spt.DEPARTMENT_CODE, spt.DEPARTMENT_NAME, spt.TERM_CODE, spt.num_subjects FROM subjects_per_term spt WHERE spt.DEPARTMENT_CODE IN (SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE FROM dept_terms) ), ranked_terms AS ( SELECT icte.DEPARTMENT_CODE, icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, icte.TERM_CODE, icte.num_subjects, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY icte.DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY icte.num_subjects DESC, icte.TERM_CODE) AS term_rank FROM inner_cte icte ), agg_stats AS ( SELECT icte.DEPARTMENT_CODE, icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(icte.num_subjects) - MIN(icte.num_subjects) AS range_num_subjects, VARIANCE(icte.num_subjects) AS variance_num_subjects, STDDEV(icte.num_subjects) AS stddev_num_subjects FROM inner_cte icte GROUP BY icte.DEPARTMENT_CODE, icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT a.DEPARTMENT_NAME, a.range_num_subjects, a.variance_num_subjects, a.stddev_num_subjects, r.TERM_CODE AS term_with_most_subjects, r.num_subjects AS num_subjects_in_term FROM agg_stats a JOIN ranked_terms r ON a.DEPARTMENT_CODE = r.DEPARTMENT_CODE AND r.term_rank = 1 ORDER BY a.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of subjects offered per term by that department, considering only departments that are degree granting, have offered at least one subject in the term '2016SP', and are not the Chemistry department.
sub_sqls: WITH dept_terms AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING, sos.TERM_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.TERM_CODE = '2016SP' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Chemistry' ), subjects_per_term AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sos.TERM_CODE, COUNT(sos.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_subjects FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Chemistry' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sos.TERM_CODE ) SELECT spt.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(spt.num_subjects) - MIN(spt.num_subjects) AS range_num_subjects, VARIANCE(spt.num_subjects) AS variance_num_subjects, STDDEV(spt.num_subjects) AS stddev_num_subjects FROM subjects_per_term spt WHERE spt.DEPARTMENT_CODE IN (SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE FROM dept_terms) GROUP BY spt.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY spt.DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: For each school, provide the school name and calculate the average and variance of the total units for subjects offered by departments in that school in the 2022 academic year, but only include schools where all departments grant degrees and exclude any school that contains the Biology department (Course 7). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.SCHOOL_CODE, d.SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_units, VARIANCE(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS units_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE s.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '7' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.SCHOOL_CODE, d.SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT ic.SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(ic.avg_units) AS school_avg_units, VARIANCE(ic.avg_units) AS school_units_variance FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME = d.DEPARTMENT_NAME AND ic.SCHOOL_CODE = d.SCHOOL_CODE WHERE d.SCHOOL_CODE NOT IN ( SELECT SCHOOL_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE = '7' ) GROUP BY ic.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY school_units_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, provide the department name and calculate the average and variance of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the 2022 academic year, but only include departments that grant degrees and exclude the Biology department (Course 7).
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_units, VARIANCE(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS units_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE s.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '7' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY units_variance DESC;

question: For each Mathematics department subject offered in the term '2019FA' that has course materials, list the subject title, number of enrolled students, responsible faculty name, the department name, and the school name. Also, include a dense rank over the department name, ordered by department name. Do not repeat the department name if it is the same as the previous row. Sort the table by department name and subject title. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t0.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, t0.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.SCHOOL_NAME, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS window_column FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT t1 ON t0.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION t2 ON t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t2.DEPARTMENT WHERE t0.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND t0.IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL = 'N' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(DEPARTMENT_NAME) OVER (ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUBJECT_TITLE) = DEPARTMENT_NAME THEN NULL ELSE DEPARTMENT_NAME END AS department_name, SUBJECT_TITLE, NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, window_column FROM inner_cte ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUBJECT_TITLE;
sub_questions: List the subject title, number of enrolled students, and the responsible faculty name for each subject offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18) in the term '2019FA', where the subject has course materials, along with a dense rank over the department name, ordered by department name.

question: From the top 10 departments with the highest average total units for their subjects (considering only subjects with more than 0 total units), display each department's name, the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of total units, the school most represented among those subjects, and the count of subjects from that school. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.SCHOOL_NAME, sos.TOTAL_UNITS FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON scd.COURSE = sos.COURSE_NUMBER WHERE sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 ) SELECT d_stats.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d_stats.avg_total_units, d_stats.stddev_total_units, s_stats.Most_Prominent_School, s_stats.Subject_Count FROM ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME ) d_stats LEFT JOIN ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME AS Most_Prominent_School, Subject_Count, @rank := IF(@current_dept = DEPARTMENT_NAME, @rank + 1, 1) AS `Rank`, @current_dept := DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(*) AS Subject_Count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME ) s CROSS JOIN (SELECT @rank := 0, @current_dept := '') vars ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, Subject_Count DESC ) s_stats ON d_stats.DEPARTMENT_NAME = s_stats.DEPARTMENT_NAME AND s_stats.`Rank` = 1 ORDER BY d_stats.avg_total_units DESC LIMIT 10;
sub_questions: For each department, provide the department name and calculate the average and standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, considering only subjects with more than 0 total units, and restrict the results to the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON scd.COURSE = sos.COURSE_NUMBER WHERE sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND scd.DEPARTMENT = '18' GROUP BY scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY stddev_total_units DESC;

question: For each subject offered in the Mathematics department (Course 18) that has more than 0 enrolled students and is in a degree-granting department, list the department name, subject title, number of enrolled students, and school name, along with a dense rank over the department code ordered by department code, but only include those subjects where the number of enrolled students is greater than the average number of enrolled students for all subjects in the Mathematics department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, t2.SCHOOL_NAME, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS window_column FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN STUDENT_DEPARTMENT t2 ON t1.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = t2.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND t0.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUBJECT_TITLE, NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, SCHOOL_NAME, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > ( SELECT AVG(t1.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' AND t1.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND t0.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' )
sub_questions: List the department name, subject title, number of enrolled students, and school name for each subject offered, along with dense ranks over the department code ordered by department code, for subjects with more than 0 enrolled students in departments that grant degrees, specifically for the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, t2.SCHOOL_NAME, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS window_column FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN STUDENT_DEPARTMENT t2 ON t1.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = t2.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND t0.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18'

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding the Physics department, Course 8), provide the department name, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the 2022 academic year, and the average number of enrolled students for those subjects, but only include departments with more than one subject offered in 2022. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '8' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 1 ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.coefficient_of_variation, AVG(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrolled_students FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE tso.TERM_CODE LIKE '2022%' GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.coefficient_of_variation ORDER BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the coefficient of variation of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the 2022 academic year, but only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the Physics department (Course 8).
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '8' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 1 ORDER BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For each degree-granting department with a department budget code above 100000, excluding the Political Science department, provide the department code, department name, school name, the number of unique courses offered by the department, the total number of units for all those courses, and the number of those courses that are cross-listed in the SIS_SUBJECT_CODE table (i.e., have a matching SUBJECT_CODE in SIS_SUBJECT_CODE). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.SUBJECT_CODE) AS num_unique_courses, SUM(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG c ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = c.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE > 100000 AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '17' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.SCHOOL_NAME, ic.num_unique_courses, ic.total_units, COUNT(DISTINCT ssc.SUBJECT_CODE) AS num_crosslisted_courses FROM inner_cte ic JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE LEFT JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON ccc.SUBJECT_CODE = ssc.SUBJECT_CODE GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.SCHOOL_NAME, ic.num_unique_courses, ic.total_units ORDER BY ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE;
sub_questions: For each department that is degree-granting, has a department budget code above 100000, and is not the Political Science department, give the department code, department name, school name, the number of unique courses offered by the department, and the total number of units for all those courses, excluding the Political Science department (Course 17).
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.SUBJECT_CODE) AS num_unique_courses, SUM(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG c ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = c.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE > 100000 AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '17' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE ;

question: For each building type and campus sector, which buildings have an assignable area greater than the average assignable area for their group, considering only buildings with more than 10 rooms, a non-null building use, and that are residential buildings, using both the current and historical building data, and only including buildings that are owned? Return the building type, campus sector, building number, and assignable area. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT BUILDING_TYPE, CAMPUS_SECTOR, BUILDING_NUMBER, ASSIGNABLE_AREA FROM FCLT_BUILDING WHERE NUM_OF_ROOMS > 10 AND BUILDING_USE IS NOT NULL AND BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'OWNED' UNION ALL SELECT BUILDING_TYPE, CAMPUS_SECTOR, BUILDING_NUMBER, ASSIGNABLE_AREA FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST WHERE NUM_OF_ROOMS > 10 AND BUILDING_USE IS NOT NULL AND BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'OWNED' ), group_avgs AS ( SELECT BUILDING_TYPE, CAMPUS_SECTOR, AVG(ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS avg_assignable_area FROM inner_cte GROUP BY BUILDING_TYPE, CAMPUS_SECTOR ) SELECT i.BUILDING_TYPE, i.CAMPUS_SECTOR, i.BUILDING_NUMBER, i.ASSIGNABLE_AREA FROM inner_cte i JOIN group_avgs g ON i.BUILDING_TYPE = g.BUILDING_TYPE AND i.CAMPUS_SECTOR = g.CAMPUS_SECTOR WHERE i.ASSIGNABLE_AREA > g.avg_assignable_area;
sub_questions: For each building type and campus sector, what are the average, variance, and standard deviation of the assignable area for buildings, considering only buildings with more than 10 rooms, a non-null building use, and that are residential buildings, using both the current and historical building data, and only including buildings that are owned?
sub_sqls: SELECT BUILDING_TYPE, CAMPUS_SECTOR, AVG(ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS avg_assignable_area, VARIANCE(ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS var_assignable_area, STDDEV(ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS stddev_assignable_area FROM ( SELECT BUILDING_TYPE, CAMPUS_SECTOR, ASSIGNABLE_AREA FROM FCLT_BUILDING WHERE NUM_OF_ROOMS > 10 AND BUILDING_USE IS NOT NULL AND BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'OWNED' UNION ALL SELECT BUILDING_TYPE, CAMPUS_SECTOR, ASSIGNABLE_AREA FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST WHERE NUM_OF_ROOMS > 10 AND BUILDING_USE IS NOT NULL AND BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'OWNED' ) AS all_buildings GROUP BY BUILDING_TYPE, CAMPUS_SECTOR;

question: For each academic building at MIT with more than 3 historical records and a nonzero assignable area, what is the building name, the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the assignable area across its historical records, the current assignable area, and the deviation of the current assignable area from the historical average? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.BUILDING_NAME, b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, STDDEV(h.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS assignable_area_stddev, AVG(h.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS avg_assignable_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING b JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_HIST h ON b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = h.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE h.ASSIGNABLE_AREA > 0 AND b.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND b.SITE = 'MIT' GROUP BY b.BUILDING_NAME, b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY HAVING COUNT(*) > 3 ) SELECT i.BUILDING_NAME, i.assignable_area_stddev, b.ASSIGNABLE_AREA AS current_assignable_area, (b.ASSIGNABLE_AREA - i.avg_assignable_area) AS deviation_from_historical_avg FROM FCLT_BUILDING b JOIN inner_cte i ON b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = i.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY i.assignable_area_stddev DESC;
sub_questions: For each building, what is the building name and the standard deviation of the assignable area across its historical records, considering only buildings with more than 3 historical records, with a nonzero assignable area, and that are academic buildings? Additionally, restrict the results to buildings at MIT.
sub_sqls: SELECT b.BUILDING_NAME, STDDEV(h.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS assignable_area_stddev FROM FCLT_BUILDING b JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_HIST h ON b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = h.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE h.ASSIGNABLE_AREA > 0 AND b.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND b.SITE = 'MIT' GROUP BY b.BUILDING_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 3 ORDER BY assignable_area_stddev DESC;

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding Chemistry), what is the department name, the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department (considering only subjects with more than 0 total units), and how many unique students are in those departments according to the MIT student directory? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.avg_total_units, inner_cte.stddev_total_units, COUNT(DISTINCT msd.FULL_NAME) AS num_students FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT GROUP BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.avg_total_units, inner_cte.stddev_total_units ORDER BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name, and what are the average and standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, considering only subjects with more than 0 total units and departments that are degree granting, but excluding the Chemistry department (Course 5)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: For buildings located in the city of CAMBRIDGE with a non-zero assignable area on their floors, and that are academic buildings, show the building name, building number, floor number, assignable area, building address postal code, the total number of floors per building, and assign row numbers within each postal code group ordered by building number. Additionally, restrict the results to buildings that are Maclaurin Buildings. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t2.BUILDING_NAME, t2.BUILDING_NUMBER, t1.FLOOR, t1.ASSIGNABLE_AREA, t0.POSTAL_CODE, t2.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS t0 JOIN FCLT_FLOOR t1 ON t0.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = t1.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING t2 ON t1.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = t2.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE t0.CITY = 'CAMBRIDGE' AND t1.ASSIGNABLE_AREA > 0 AND t2.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND t2.BUILDING_NAME = 'MACLAURIN BUILDINGS (3)' ) SELECT inner_cte.BUILDING_NAME, inner_cte.BUILDING_NUMBER, inner_cte.FLOOR, inner_cte.ASSIGNABLE_AREA, inner_cte.POSTAL_CODE, FloorCounts.Total_Floors, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inner_cte.POSTAL_CODE ORDER BY inner_cte.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT t2.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, COUNT(DISTINCT t1.FLOOR) AS Total_Floors FROM FCLT_BUILDING t2 JOIN FCLT_FLOOR t1 ON t2.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = t1.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY GROUP BY t2.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ) AS FloorCounts ON inner_cte.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = FloorCounts.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY;
sub_questions: For buildings located in the city of CAMBRIDGE with a non-zero assignable area on their floors, and that are academic buildings, show the building name, building number, floor number, assignable area, building address postal code, and assign row numbers within each postal code group ordered by building number. Additionally, restrict the results to buildings that are Maclaurin Buildings.
sub_sqls: SELECT t2.BUILDING_NAME, t2.BUILDING_NUMBER, t1.FLOOR, t1.ASSIGNABLE_AREA, t0.POSTAL_CODE, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.POSTAL_CODE ORDER BY t2.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS window_column FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS t0 JOIN FCLT_FLOOR t1 ON t0.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = t1.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING t2 ON t1.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = t2.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE t0.CITY = 'CAMBRIDGE' AND t1.ASSIGNABLE_AREA > 0 AND t2.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND t2.BUILDING_NAME = 'MACLAURIN BUILDINGS (3)'

question: For each city, list the city name and, for each building in that city that is used as a residence (excluding the Stata building), show the building number and its external gross area, but only include buildings whose external gross area is above the average for residential buildings in that city. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fba.CITY AS city_name, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.BUILDING_NUMBER, fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY <> '32' ) , city_avg AS ( SELECT city_name, AVG(EXT_GROSS_AREA) AS avg_ext_gross_area FROM inner_cte GROUP BY city_name ) SELECT i.city_name, i.BUILDING_NUMBER, i.EXT_GROSS_AREA FROM inner_cte i JOIN city_avg a ON i.city_name = a.city_name WHERE i.EXT_GROSS_AREA > a.avg_ext_gross_area ORDER BY i.city_name, i.BUILDING_NUMBER ;
domain_knowledge: "used as a residence" is predicated by "TABLE.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT'"
sub_questions: For each city, give the city name and find the average and standard deviation of the external gross area of buildings that have at least one address in that city, but only include buildings that are used as a residence and exclude buildings in the Stata building.
sub_sqls: SELECT fba.CITY AS city_name, AVG(fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA) AS avg_ext_gross_area, STDDEV(fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA) AS stddev_ext_gross_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' AND fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY <> '32' GROUP BY fba.CITY ORDER BY fba.CITY ;

question: For each building address in the city of Cambridge, show the building number, address purpose, city, state, postal code, the building name, building type, building use, and the maximum number of rooms from the building history for the current row and the next 2 rows ordered by building key, but only include buildings that are academic buildings. For each building name and building type, include a grand total for all rows in the format of (building name, building type, null, total max number of rooms). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fba.BUILDING_NUMBER, fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE, fba.CITY, fba.STATE, fba.POSTAL_CODE, fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_TYPE, fb.BUILDING_USE, fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fbh.FISCAL_PERIOD, GREATEST( fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS, COALESCE(LEAD(fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fbh.FISCAL_PERIOD), 0), COALESCE(LEAD(fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fbh.FISCAL_PERIOD), 0) ) AS max_num_of_rooms_3rows FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fba.CITY = 'Cambridge' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' ), RollupResults AS ( SELECT BUILDING_NAME, BUILDING_TYPE, ADDRESS_PURPOSE, SUM(max_num_of_rooms_3rows) AS total_max_num_of_rooms FROM inner_cte GROUP BY BUILDING_NAME, BUILDING_TYPE, ADDRESS_PURPOSE WITH ROLLUP HAVING SUM(max_num_of_rooms_3rows) > 0 ) SELECT rr.BUILDING_NAME, rr.BUILDING_TYPE, rr.ADDRESS_PURPOSE, rr.total_max_num_of_rooms FROM RollupResults rr ORDER BY rr.BUILDING_NAME, rr.BUILDING_TYPE, rr.ADDRESS_PURPOSE
domain_knowledge: "Cambridge" is a city in Massachusetts and is the primary location of MIT's campus, so filtering by t0.CITY = 'Cambridge' is a reasonable external constraint.
sub_questions: For each building address in the city of Cambridge, show the building number, address purpose, city, state, postal code, the building name, building type, building use, and the maximum number of rooms from the building history for the current row and the next 2 rows ordered by building key, but only include buildings that are academic buildings.
sub_sqls: WITH building_hist_stats AS ( SELECT fba.BUILDING_NUMBER, fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE, fba.CITY, fba.STATE, fba.POSTAL_CODE, fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_TYPE, fb.BUILDING_USE, fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fbh.FISCAL_PERIOD, GREATEST( fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS, COALESCE(LEAD(fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fbh.FISCAL_PERIOD), 0), COALESCE(LEAD(fbh.NUM_OF_ROOMS, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fbh.FISCAL_PERIOD), 0) ) AS max_num_of_rooms_3rows FROM FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fba.CITY = 'Cambridge' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' ) SELECT BUILDING_NUMBER, ADDRESS_PURPOSE, CITY, STATE, POSTAL_CODE, BUILDING_NAME, BUILDING_TYPE, BUILDING_USE, max_num_of_rooms_3rows FROM building_hist_stats ORDER BY FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, FISCAL_PERIOD;

question: For each degree-granting department in the School of Engineering (excluding the Department of Management, Course 15), what is the maximum total units of any course offered by that department in the 2008 academic year, along with the subject code, subject code description, and the graduate level of that course? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units, c.SUBJECT_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG c ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = c.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND c.ACADEMIC_YEAR = '2008' AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '15' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.SUBJECT_CODE HAVING MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.max_total_units, inner_cte.SUBJECT_CODE, sc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, scd.GRADUATE_LEVEL FROM inner_cte JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE sc ON inner_cte.SUBJECT_CODE = sc.SUBJECT_CODE JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sc.SUBJECT_CODE = scd.COURSE
sub_questions: For each department in the School of Engineering that is degree-granting, what is the maximum total units of any course offered by that department in the 2008 academic year, and what is the subject code of that course? Exclude the Department of Management (Course 15) from the results.
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units, c.SUBJECT_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG c ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = c.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND c.ACADEMIC_YEAR = '2008' AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '15' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.SUBJECT_CODE HAVING MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0;

question: For courses in the School of Engineering that are degree granting and are in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, show the course, course description, department name, program title, and rank within each department name group ordered by course, but only include those where the program title contains the word 'Engineering'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t1.COURSE, t1.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.PROGRAM_TITLE, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t1.COURSE) window_column FROM CIP t0 JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION t1 ON t0.PROGRAM_CODE = t1.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE WHERE t1.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND t1.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' ) SELECT * FROM inner_cte WHERE PROGRAM_TITLE LIKE '%Engineering%'

"Course 6" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
sub_questions: For courses in the School of Engineering that are degree granting and are in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, show the course, course description, department name, program title, and rank within each department name group ordered by course.
sub_sqls: SELECT t1.COURSE, t1.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.PROGRAM_TITLE, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t1.COURSE) window_column FROM CIP t0 JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION t1 ON t0.PROGRAM_CODE = t1.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE WHERE t1.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND t1.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'

question: For each department, provide the department name, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the 2022 academic year, the school name, and the department phone number. Only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the 'Political Science' department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation, sd.SCHOOL_NAME, ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME LEFT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ad ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the coefficient of variation of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the 2022 academic year, but only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the 'Political Science' department.

question: For each academic year, provide the academic year description, and for subjects offered in current terms by the Mathematics department (Course 18), show the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of total units, along with the number of such subjects and the maximum total units offered in any subject that year. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, AVG(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ON COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.TERM_CODE JOIN ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER ON ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER.TERM_CODE WHERE ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, inner_cte.avg_total_units, inner_cte.stddev_total_units, COUNT(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_subjects, MAX(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units FROM inner_cte JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ON inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR = ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.ACADEMIC_YEAR JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.TERM_CODE AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER ON ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER.TERM_CODE AND ACADEMIC_TERM_PARAMETER.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' GROUP BY inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR, inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, inner_cte.avg_total_units, inner_cte.stddev_total_units ORDER BY inner_cte.stddev_total_units DESC;

question: For subjects offered in the term '2016SP' with a total number of units greater than 1, in the Political Science department, show the subject ID, subject title, department name, and the running sum of total units within each school name group, along with the school name and subject code description, ordered by subject ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sos.SUBJECT_ID, sos.SUBJECT_TITLE, scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) OVER (PARTITION BY sos.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY sos.SUBJECT_ID ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_sum_total_units, sos.COURSE_NUMBER FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sos.COURSE_NUMBER = scd.COURSE WHERE sos.TERM_CODE = '2016SP' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 1 AND scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' ) SELECT i.SUBJECT_ID, i.SUBJECT_TITLE, i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.running_sum_total_units, scd2.SCHOOL_NAME, ssc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC FROM inner_cte i JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd2 ON i.COURSE_NUMBER = scd2.COURSE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON i.COURSE_NUMBER = ssc.COURSE_NUMBER ORDER BY i.SUBJECT_ID;
sub_questions: For subjects offered in the term '2016SP' with a total number of units greater than 1, in the Political Science department, show the subject ID, subject title, department name, and the running sum of total units within each school name group, ordered by subject ID.

question: For each subject offered in the 2022 academic year by the Mathematics department, what is the maximum number of total units for that subject, the department name from the course catalog, and the number of times each subject was offered in that year, considering only subjects where the maximum total units is greater than 6? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, MAX(cso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units, ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON cso.SUBJECT_ID = ccc.SUBJECT_ID WHERE cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING MAX(cso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 6 ) SELECT inner_cte.SUBJECT_TITLE, inner_cte.max_total_units, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, subj_count.subject_offered_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, COUNT(*) AS subject_offered_count FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON cso.SUBJECT_ID = ccc.SUBJECT_ID WHERE cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY cso.SUBJECT_TITLE ) subj_count ON inner_cte.SUBJECT_TITLE = subj_count.SUBJECT_TITLE;
sub_questions: For each subject offered in the 2022 academic year by the Mathematics department, what is the maximum number of total units for that subject, and what is the department name from the course catalog, considering only subjects where the maximum total units is greater than 6?
sub_sqls: SELECT cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, MAX(cso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units, ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON cso.SUBJECT_ID = ccc.SUBJECT_ID WHERE cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, ccc.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING MAX(cso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 6;

question: List the minimum department code and the total number of unique department names for degree-granting courses in the School of Engineering, excluding courses from the Physics department, along with the corresponding subject code descriptions. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIN(ssc.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS min_department_code, COUNT(DISTINCT ssc.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS total_unique_departments FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON ssc.SUBJECT_CODE = scd.COURSE WHERE scd.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ssc.DEPARTMENT_NAME != 'Physics' ) SELECT inner_cte.min_department_code, inner_cte.total_unique_departments, ssc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC FROM inner_cte JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON ssc.DEPARTMENT_CODE = inner_cte.min_department_code;

question: Show the organization names, their DLC names, the number of distinct HR organizational units, and the total number of unique HR department names per organization, for the top 3 organizations (by number of HR organizational units), excluding organizations '138' and '250', and only including organizations whose DLC name is 'Biology'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, hou.DLC_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT hou.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID) AS num_hr_org_units FROM FCLT_ORGANIZATION fo JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT hou ON fo.DLC_KEY = hou.DLC_KEY WHERE fo.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN (138, 250) AND LOWER(hou.DLC_NAME) = 'biology' GROUP BY fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, hou.DLC_NAME ORDER BY num_hr_org_units DESC, fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME LIMIT 3 ) SELECT icte.ORGANIZATION_NAME, icte.DLC_NAME, icte.num_hr_org_units, COUNT(DISTINCT hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS num_hr_departments FROM inner_cte icte JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION fo ON icte.ORGANIZATION_NAME = fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AND icte.DLC_NAME = fo.DLC_NAME JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT hou ON fo.DLC_KEY = hou.DLC_KEY WHERE LOWER(hou.DLC_NAME) = 'biology' GROUP BY icte.ORGANIZATION_NAME, icte.DLC_NAME, icte.num_hr_org_units ORDER BY icte.num_hr_org_units DESC, icte.ORGANIZATION_NAME;
