question: For each department, what are the top 10 material statuses by the number of materials for courses in that department, including the material status description and the count of materials for each status, considering only courses with materials, and only include departments where the total number of materials is greater than the average number of materials across all departments? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS department_name, tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS material_status_description, COUNT(td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS material_count FROM TIP_DETAIL td JOIN TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS tms ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON td.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID AND td.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE WHERE (td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY IS NOT NULL AND td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY NOT LIKE 'N/ACourse has no materials%') GROUP BY ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS ) SELECT department_name, material_status_description, material_count FROM ( SELECT department_name, material_status_description, material_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department_name ORDER BY material_count DESC) AS rn FROM inner_cte ) ranked WHERE rn <= 10 AND department_name IN ( SELECT department_name FROM ( SELECT department_name, SUM(material_count) AS total_materials FROM inner_cte GROUP BY department_name ) dept_totals WHERE total_materials > ( SELECT AVG(total_materials) FROM ( SELECT department_name, SUM(material_count) AS total_materials FROM inner_cte GROUP BY department_name ) all_depts ) ) ORDER BY department_name, material_count DESC;
sub_questions: What are the top 10 material statuses by the number of materials for courses in the Biology department, including the material status description and the count of materials for each status, considering only courses with materials?
sub_sqls: SELECT tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS material_status_description, COUNT(td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS material_count FROM TIP_DETAIL td JOIN TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS tms ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON td.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID AND td.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Biology' AND (td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY IS NOT NULL AND td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY NOT LIKE 'N/ACourse has no materials%') GROUP BY tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS ORDER BY material_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each department, provide the department name, the average and variance of the number of enrolled students in courses that have at least one associated material record and are from the Chemistry department, and also show the total number of such courses for each department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, AVG(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrollment, VARIANCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrollment_variance FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON tso.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE WHERE td.RECORD_COUNT > 0 AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Chemistry' GROUP BY tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME ) SELECT i.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, i.avg_enrollment, i.enrollment_variance, COUNT(tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY) AS total_courses FROM inner_cte i JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = i.OFFER_DEPT_NAME JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON tso.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE WHERE td.RECORD_COUNT > 0 AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Chemistry' GROUP BY i.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, i.avg_enrollment, i.enrollment_variance ORDER BY i.enrollment_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, provide the department name and calculate the average and variance of the number of enrolled students in courses that have at least one associated material record, but only include courses from the Chemistry department (Course 5).
sub_sqls: SELECT tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, AVG(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrollment, VARIANCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrollment_variance FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON tso.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE WHERE td.RECORD_COUNT > 0 AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Chemistry' GROUP BY tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME ORDER BY enrollment_variance DESC;

question: List each administrative department's name, the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units of courses offered by that department (only for degree-granting departments, courses with total units greater than 0, and excluding the Mechanical Engineering department), along with the total number of such courses per department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, ccc.TOTAL_UNITS FROM SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccc.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND UPPER(sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) <> 'MECHANICAL ENGINEERING' ) SELECT icte.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(icte.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(icte.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(icte.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev, dept_course_counts.Total_Courses FROM inner_cte icte JOIN ( SELECT SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(*) AS Total_Courses FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ) AS dept_course_counts ON icte.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME = dept_course_counts.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME GROUP BY icte.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, dept_course_counts.Total_Courses ORDER BY total_units_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each administrative department, what is the average, variance, and standard deviation of the total units of courses offered by that department, considering only departments that grant degrees, courses with total units greater than 0, and excluding the Mechanical Engineering department (Course 2)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, VARIANCE(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccc.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND UPPER(sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) <> 'MECHANICAL ENGINEERING' GROUP BY sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY total_units_variance DESC;

question: For each department name and course level where the department is degree granting and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique students and the minimum CIP program code among their courses. Additionally, for each department name, include a grand total of unique students and the minimum CIP program code across all course levels in the format of (department name, null, total students, min CIP code). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.COURSE_LEVEL, COUNT(DISTINCT msd.FULL_NAME) AS student_count, MIN(scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS min_cip_code FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON scd.DEPARTMENT = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.COURSE_LEVEL ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, COURSE_LEVEL, SUM(student_count) AS total_students, MIN(min_cip_code) AS min_cip_code FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, COURSE_LEVEL WITH ROLLUP HAVING SUM(student_count) > 0 ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, COURSE_LEVEL
sub_questions: For each department name and course level where the department is degree granting and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique students and the minimum CIP program code among their courses.
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.COURSE_LEVEL, COUNT(DISTINCT msd.FULL_NAME) AS student_count, MIN(scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS min_cip_code FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON scd.DEPARTMENT = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.COURSE_LEVEL;

question: For each department, list the department name and the number of degree-granting subjects it offered in the term '2014FA' that had more than 5 students enrolled. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS econ_subjects_with_5plus_students, scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON scd.COURSE = ssc.COURSE_NUMBER JOIN LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED lso ON ssc.COURSE_NUMBER = lso.COURSE_NUMBER WHERE lso.TERM_CODE = '2014FA' AND lso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 5 AND scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' GROUP BY scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, econ_subjects_with_5plus_students FROM inner_cte;
sub_questions: Count how many subjects offered in the term '2014FA' by the Department of Economics (Course 14) that are degree-granting had more than 5 students enrolled.
sub_sqls: SELECT COUNT(*) AS econ_subjects_with_5plus_students FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON scd.COURSE = ssc.COURSE_NUMBER JOIN LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED lso ON ssc.COURSE_NUMBER = lso.COURSE_NUMBER WHERE lso.TERM_CODE = '2014FA' AND lso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Economics' AND lso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 5 AND scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Economics'

question: For each building, provide the building name, the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the assignable area of its floors, and the total number of rooms, considering only buildings that have more than one floor, are located on the MIT site, and are academic buildings. Additionally, exclude the Brown Building (building key 39) from the results. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.BUILDING_NAME, AVG(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS avg_assignable_area, STDDEV(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS stddev_assignable_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING fb JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.SITE = 'MIT' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY <> '39' GROUP BY fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.BUILDING_NAME HAVING COUNT(ff.FCLT_FLOOR_KEY) > 1 ) SELECT ic.BUILDING_NAME, ic.avg_assignable_area, ic.stddev_assignable_area, fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS FROM inner_cte ic JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON ic.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY ic.BUILDING_NAME;
sub_questions: For each building, give the building name and find the average and standard deviation of the assignable area of its floors, considering only buildings that have more than one floor, are located on the MIT site, and are academic buildings. Additionally, exclude the Brown Building (building key 39) from the results.
sub_sqls: SELECT fb.BUILDING_NAME, AVG(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS avg_assignable_area, STDDEV(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS stddev_assignable_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING fb JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.SITE = 'MIT' AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY <> '39' GROUP BY fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.BUILDING_NAME HAVING COUNT(ff.FCLT_FLOOR_KEY) > 1 ORDER BY fb.BUILDING_NAME ;

question: For each student year and department, provide the student year, department name, the average, range, and variance of department budget codes for students in that year and department, considering only students whose department code matches both an academic department and an administrative department, and who are in a degree-granting department. Include subtotals for each student year (the corresponding student year field is 'SUBTOTAL') and a grand total across all years (the corresponding student year field is 'TOTAL'). Do not repeat the student year if it is the same as the previous row. Sort the table by student year and department name. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR, SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ON MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT = SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(student_year) OVER (ORDER BY year_sort, student_year, dept_sort) = student_year THEN NULL ELSE student_year END AS student_year, department_name, avg_budget, budget_range, budget_variance FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(STUDENT_YEAR) = 1 AND GROUPING(DEPARTMENT_NAME) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE STUDENT_YEAR END AS year_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(STUDENT_YEAR) = 0 AND GROUPING(DEPARTMENT_NAME) = 1 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(STUDENT_YEAR) = 1 AND GROUPING(DEPARTMENT_NAME) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE STUDENT_YEAR END AS student_year, CASE WHEN GROUPING(STUDENT_YEAR) = 0 AND GROUPING(DEPARTMENT_NAME) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE DEPARTMENT_NAME END AS dept_sort, DEPARTMENT_NAME AS department_name, AVG(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_budget, MAX(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_range, VARIANCE(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_variance FROM inner_cte GROUP BY STUDENT_YEAR, DEPARTMENT_NAME WITH ROLLUP ) tbl ORDER BY year_sort, dept_sort;
sub_questions: For each student year, give the student year and calculate the average, range, and variance of department budget codes for students in that year, considering only students whose department code matches both an academic department and an administrative department, and who are in the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR, AVG(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_budget, MAX(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_range, VARIANCE(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ON MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT = SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR ORDER BY budget_range DESC;

question: For each department, what is the department name, the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department (considering only subjects with more than 0 total units and departments that are degree granting, but excluding the Chemistry department), and the number of graduate students in that department? Only include departments that have at least one graduate student. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.avg_total_units, ic.stddev_total_units, COUNT(msd.FULL_NAME) AS num_grad_students FROM inner_cte ic JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE msd.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.avg_total_units, ic.stddev_total_units HAVING COUNT(msd.FULL_NAME) > 0 ORDER BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name, and what are the average and standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, considering only subjects with more than 0 total units and departments that are degree granting, but excluding the Chemistry department (Course 5)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: List the minimum number of enrolled students in any subject, the total number of degree-granting courses, and the corresponding department names for departments in the School of Engineering, specifically excluding the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIN(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS min_num_enrolled_students, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' THEN scd.COURSE END) AS total_degree_granting_courses, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = scd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.min_num_enrolled_students, inner_cte.total_degree_granting_courses FROM inner_cte;
domain_knowledge: "Computer Science" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
"Electrical Engineering and Computer Science" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
sub_questions: What is the minimum number of enrolled students in any subject and the total number of degree-granting courses offered by departments in the School of Engineering, specifically excluding the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science department?
sub_sqls: SELECT MIN(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS min_num_enrolled_students, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN scd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' THEN scd.COURSE END) AS total_degree_granting_courses FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = scd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' ;

question: For each DLC, list the DLC key, DLC name, the number of unique organizations, and the total number of assignable organizations, along with the department name and department code for each DLC. Only include DLCs that have at least one assignable organization, whose DLC name contains the word 'Office', and that are not the biology department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DLC_KEY, o.DLC_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT o.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS organization_count, SUM(CASE WHEN o.ASSIGNABLE = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS assignable_organization_count FROM FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY d JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION o ON d.DLC_KEY = o.DLC_KEY WHERE o.ASSIGNABLE = 1 AND o.DLC_NAME LIKE '%Office%' AND LOWER(o.DLC_NAME) != LOWER('Biology') GROUP BY d.DLC_KEY, o.DLC_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.DLC_KEY, inner_cte.DLC_NAME, inner_cte.organization_count, inner_cte.assignable_organization_count, fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS department_name, fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD AS department_code FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION fo ON inner_cte.DLC_KEY = fo.DLC_KEY AND fo.ASSIGNABLE = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.DLC_KEY, fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
domain_knowledge: "Departments, Laboratories, and Centers" are abbreviated by "DLCs"
sub_questions: For each DLC, what is the DLC key, DLC name, the number of unique organizations, and the total number of assignable organizations, considering only DLCs that have at least one assignable organization, whose DLC name contains the word 'Office', and that are not the biology department?
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DLC_KEY, o.DLC_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT o.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS organization_count, SUM(CASE WHEN o.ASSIGNABLE = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS assignable_organization_count FROM FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY d JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION o ON d.DLC_KEY = o.DLC_KEY WHERE o.ASSIGNABLE = 1 AND o.DLC_NAME LIKE '%Office%' AND LOWER(o.DLC_NAME) != LOWER('Biology') GROUP BY d.DLC_KEY, o.DLC_NAME;

question: Among all departments, for each academic year after 2000, which department offered the highest number of subjects with more than 0 total units, and what are the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units of those subjects in that year? Show the academic year, academic year description, department name, number of such subjects, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(*) AS subject_count, VARIANCE(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ss.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE WHERE ss.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND at.ACADEMIC_YEAR > 2000 GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT ic.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ic.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.subject_count, ic.total_units_variance, ic.total_units_stddev FROM ( SELECT inner_cte.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY inner_cte.subject_count DESC) AS rn FROM inner_cte ) ic WHERE ic.rn = 1 ORDER BY ic.ACADEMIC_YEAR;
sub_questions: For each academic year after 2000, what is the academic year description, and what are the variance and standard deviation of the total units of subjects offered in that year, considering only subjects with more than 0 total units, that are offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, VARIANCE(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ss.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE WHERE ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ss.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND at.ACADEMIC_YEAR > 2000 GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ORDER BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR

question: Among all academic buildings at MIT with more than 10 rooms (excluding those named 'Ray and Maria Stata Center'), which building has the highest total assignable area in its building history? For that building, show its building key, building name, building type, number of historical records, total assignable area, and the fiscal period with the maximum assignable area along with that value. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_TYPE, COUNT(fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_HIST_KEY) AS num_historical_records, SUM(fbh.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS total_assignable_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING fb JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AND fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE = fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE WHERE fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS > 10 AND fb.SITE = 'MIT' AND fb.BUILDING_NAME <> 'Ray and Maria Stata Center' AND fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY <> '32' GROUP BY fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_TYPE ) SELECT ic.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, ic.BUILDING_NAME, ic.BUILDING_TYPE, ic.num_historical_records, ic.total_assignable_area, fbh.FISCAL_PERIOD AS max_assignable_area_period, fbh.ASSIGNABLE_AREA AS max_assignable_area FROM inner_cte ic JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh ON ic.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AND fbh.ASSIGNABLE_AREA = ( SELECT MAX(fbh2.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) FROM FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh2 WHERE fbh2.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ic.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ) WHERE ic.total_assignable_area = ( SELECT MAX(total_assignable_area) FROM inner_cte )
domain_knowledge: "Stata building" is predicated by "TABLE.BUILDING_NAME = 'Ray and Maria Stata Center'"
sub_questions: For each building, list the building key, building name, building type, the number of historical records, and the total assignable area from the building history for buildings that are of type 'ACADEMIC', have more than 10 rooms, are located at MIT, and exclude buildings named 'Ray and Maria Stata Center'.
sub_sqls: SELECT fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_TYPE, COUNT(fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_HIST_KEY) AS num_historical_records, SUM(fbh.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS total_assignable_area FROM FCLT_BUILDING fb JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AND fb.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE = fbh.ACCESS_LEVEL_CODE WHERE fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS > 10 AND fb.SITE = 'MIT' AND fb.BUILDING_NAME <> 'Ray and Maria Stata Center' AND fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY <> '32' GROUP BY fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_TYPE

question: For subjects offered in the term '2016SP' with a total number of units greater than 1, in the Political Science department, show the subject ID, subject title, department name, the running sum of total units within each school name group, and the corresponding subject code and subject code description, ordered by subject ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sos.SUBJECT_ID, sos.SUBJECT_TITLE, scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) OVER (PARTITION BY sos.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY sos.SUBJECT_ID ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_sum_total_units, sos.COURSE_NUMBER FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sos.COURSE_NUMBER = scd.COURSE WHERE sos.TERM_CODE = '2016SP' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 1 AND scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' ) SELECT inner_cte.SUBJECT_ID, inner_cte.SUBJECT_TITLE, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.running_sum_total_units, ssc.SUBJECT_CODE, ssc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC FROM inner_cte JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON inner_cte.COURSE_NUMBER = ssc.COURSE_NUMBER ORDER BY inner_cte.SUBJECT_ID;
sub_questions: For subjects offered in the term '2016SP' with a total number of units greater than 1, in the Political Science department, show the subject ID, subject title, department name, and the running sum of total units within each school name group, ordered by subject ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT sos.SUBJECT_ID, sos.SUBJECT_TITLE, scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) OVER (PARTITION BY sos.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY sos.SUBJECT_ID ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_sum_total_units FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sos.COURSE_NUMBER = scd.COURSE WHERE sos.TERM_CODE = '2016SP' AND sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 1 AND scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' ORDER BY sos.SUBJECT_ID;

question: For each academic year, what is the average and variance of the number of enrolled students in subjects from the Mathematics department that are offered in the fall term and have more than 0 enrolled students, but only include those academic years where the average enrollment is greater than the overall average enrollment for all such Mathematics subjects? Please show the academic year, average enrollment, and variance. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, AVG(TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrollment, VARIANCE(TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrollment_variance FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS ON COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE = TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE WHERE COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR, avg_enrollment, enrollment_variance FROM inner_cte WHERE avg_enrollment > ( SELECT AVG(TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS ON COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE = TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE WHERE COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ) ORDER BY enrollment_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the average and variance of the number of enrolled students in subjects from the Mathematics department, considering only subjects that are offered in the fall term and have more than 0 enrolled students? Please show the academic year and the calculated statistics.
sub_sqls: SELECT ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR, AVG(TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrollment, VARIANCE(TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrollment_variance FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS ON COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE = TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE WHERE COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ACADEMIC_TERMS.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY enrollment_variance DESC;

question: For each department name and school name where the student year is 'G' and the department is Mathematics (Course 18), what is the highest number of students in any office location, and what is the minimum office phone number for that department and school? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME, msd.OFFICE_LOCATION, COUNT(msd.FULL_NAME) AS student_count, MIN(msd.OFFICE_PHONE) AS min_office_phone FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE msd.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME, msd.OFFICE_LOCATION ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, MAX(student_count) AS max_students_in_office, MIN(min_office_phone) AS min_office_phone FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department name and school name where the student year is 'G' and the department is Mathematics (Course 18), give the number of students and the minimum office phone number.
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME, COUNT(msd.FULL_NAME) AS student_count, MIN(msd.OFFICE_PHONE) AS min_office_phone FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE msd.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME;

question: For each course in the School of Engineering that is degree granting and offered by the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, show the course description, department name, the department's budget code, and whether the department's budget code is 'HIGH_BUDGET' (at least 10% greater than the average budget code for Engineering departments), 'LOW_BUDGET' (at least 10% less than the average), or 'AVERAGE'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t0.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION t0 JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND t1.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' ), eng_budget_avg AS ( SELECT AVG(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_budget FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT WHERE SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL ) SELECT c.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, c.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE, CASE WHEN c.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE > e.avg_budget * 1.1 THEN 'HIGH_BUDGET' WHEN c.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE < e.avg_budget * 0.9 THEN 'LOW_BUDGET' ELSE 'AVERAGE' END AS budget_category FROM inner_cte c CROSS JOIN eng_budget_avg e;
domain_knowledge: "Computer Science" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
"Course 6" is predicated by "TABLE.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'"
sub_questions: For courses in the School of Engineering that are degree granting and are offered by the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, show the course description, department name, and the dense rank of each course considering the current and 2 preceding rows ordered by the department's budget code.
sub_sqls: SELECT t0.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, dense_rank() OVER (ORDER BY t1.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS window_column FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION t0 JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND t1.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'

question: For each department hierarchy, show the department hierarchy name, the average and variance of the organization numbers for organizations in that hierarchy where the organization is assignable, the organization level is at least 4, and exclude organizations with organization IDs '138' and '250' that are not part of the Cambridge-MIT Institute. Also, for each department hierarchy, show the total number of such organizations. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY.DLC_NAME, FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION ON MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY.DLC_KEY = FCLT_ORGANIZATION.DLC_KEY WHERE FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ASSIGNABLE = 1 AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL >= 4 AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NAME NOT IN ('CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST') ) SELECT inner_cte.DLC_NAME, AVG(inner_cte.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) AS avg_org_number, VARIANCE(inner_cte.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) AS org_number_variance, org_counts.total_orgs FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT DLC_NAME, COUNT(*) AS total_orgs FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DLC_NAME ) AS org_counts ON inner_cte.DLC_NAME = org_counts.DLC_NAME GROUP BY inner_cte.DLC_NAME, org_counts.total_orgs ORDER BY org_number_variance DESC;
domain_knowledge: "exclude organizations '138' and '250'" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250')"
"except Cambridge-MIT Institute" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_NAME NOT IN ('CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST')"
"Departments, Laboratories, and Centers" are abbreviated by "DLCs"
sub_questions: For each department hierarchy, show the department hierarchy name and calculate the average and variance of the organization numbers for organizations in that hierarchy where the organization is assignable, the organization level is at least 4, and exclude organizations with organization IDs '138' and '250' that are not part of the Cambridge-MIT Institute.
sub_sqls: SELECT MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY.DLC_NAME, AVG(FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) AS avg_org_number, VARIANCE(FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) AS org_number_variance FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION ON MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY.DLC_KEY = FCLT_ORGANIZATION.DLC_KEY WHERE FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ASSIGNABLE = 1 AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL >= 4 AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NAME NOT IN ('CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST') GROUP BY MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY.DLC_NAME ORDER BY org_number_variance DESC;

question: For each academic year, what is the academic year description, and for Mathematics department subjects offered in the fall term with at least one TIP material, what are the minimum, maximum, and average number of TIP materials per subject, along with the total number of such subjects, and the earliest and latest term start dates for those subjects in that year? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT cca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, cca.TERM_CODE, cca.SUBJECT_ID, COUNT(td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS num_tip_materials FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cca JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON cca.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE AND cca.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID WHERE cca.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND cca.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY cca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, cca.TERM_CODE, cca.SUBJECT_ID ) SELECT ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, MIN(inner_cte.num_tip_materials) AS min_tip_materials, MAX(inner_cte.num_tip_materials) AS max_tip_materials, AVG(inner_cte.num_tip_materials) AS avg_tip_materials, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.SUBJECT_ID) AS total_subjects, MIN(ata.TERM_START_DATE) AS earliest_term_start, MAX(ata.TERM_START_DATE) AS latest_term_start FROM inner_cte JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON inner_cte.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE AND inner_cte.ACADEMIC_YEAR = ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR GROUP BY ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ORDER BY ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR;
sub_questions: For each academic year, what is the academic year description, and what are the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of TIP materials per subject offered in that year, considering only subjects that are offered in the fall term, have at least one TIP material, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: WITH tip_counts AS ( SELECT cca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, cca.TERM_CODE, cca.SUBJECT_ID, COUNT(td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS num_tip_materials FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cca JOIN TIP_DETAIL td ON cca.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE AND cca.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID WHERE cca.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND cca.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY cca.ACADEMIC_YEAR, cca.TERM_CODE, cca.SUBJECT_ID ), per_year_stats AS ( SELECT ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, MIN(tc.num_tip_materials) AS min_tip_materials, MAX(tc.num_tip_materials) AS max_tip_materials, MAX(tc.num_tip_materials) - MIN(tc.num_tip_materials) AS range_tip_materials, VARIANCE(tc.num_tip_materials) AS var_tip_materials, STDDEV(tc.num_tip_materials) AS stddev_tip_materials FROM tip_counts tc JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON tc.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE AND tc.ACADEMIC_YEAR = ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR GROUP BY ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ) SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, range_tip_materials, var_tip_materials, stddev_tip_materials FROM per_year_stats ORDER BY ACADEMIC_YEAR;

question: For each department, what is the highest variance of the number of enrolled students in library subjects offered by that department across all terms, considering only departments that have at least one tip subject offered in the term '2019FA', and restricting to the Mathematics department (Course 18)? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_students_variance, STDDEV(LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_students_stddev FROM LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT ON TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(enrolled_students_variance) AS highest_enrolled_students_variance FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the variance and standard deviation of the number of enrolled students in library subjects offered by that department, considering only departments that have at least one tip subject offered in the term '2019FA', and restricting to the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_students_variance, STDDEV(LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_students_stddev FROM LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT ON TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY enrolled_students_variance DESC;

question: For each degree-granting department except Biology (Course 7), list the department name and the number of subjects offered in the 2022 academic year whose total units are above the average total units for that department in that year. Order the results by the count in descending order. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, s.TOTAL_UNITS FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE s.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '7' ) , dept_avg AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE, AVG(TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_units FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(*) AS num_subjects_above_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN dept_avg a ON i.DEPARTMENT_CODE = a.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE i.TOTAL_UNITS > a.avg_units GROUP BY i.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY num_subjects_above_avg DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, provide the department name and calculate the average and variance of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the 2022 academic year, but only include departments that grant degrees and exclude the Biology department (Course 7).
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_units, VARIANCE(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS units_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE s.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '7' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY units_variance DESC;

question: For each department and school, provide the department name, school name, and calculate the average, range, and variance of the total units for subjects offered in the 2022 academic year that are degree granting, but only include departments that are not 'Mathematics' (Course 18). Also, include the department phone number from the SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT table. Sort the results by school name and department name. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, MAX(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_range, VARIANCE(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION ON SIS_SUBJECT_CODE.COURSE_NUMBER = SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.COURSE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.COURSE = COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.SUBJECT_CODE WHERE COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Mathematics' AND SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT <> '18' GROUP BY SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME, icte.avg_total_units, icte.total_units_range, icte.total_units_variance, ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER FROM inner_cte icte LEFT JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME LEFT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ad ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY sd.SCHOOL_NAME, icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and calculate the average, range, and variance of the total units for subjects offered in the 2022 academic year that are degree granting, but only include departments that are not 'Mathematics' (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, MAX(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_range, VARIANCE(COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION ON SIS_SUBJECT_CODE.COURSE_NUMBER = SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.COURSE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.COURSE = COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.SUBJECT_CODE WHERE COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Mathematics' AND SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT <> '18' GROUP BY SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY total_units_range DESC;

question: List the department codes, department names, corresponding administrative department names, the graduate level of courses, and the total number of distinct courses per department for all degree-granting departments except the Management department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.COURSE) AS num_distinct_courses FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ad ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND UPPER(ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) <> 'MANAGEMENT' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.GRADUATE_LEVEL, ic.num_distinct_courses FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE = scd.DEPARTMENT GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, scd.GRADUATE_LEVEL, ic.num_distinct_courses;
sub_questions: Which are the top 3 departments that offer the most distinct courses, are degree-granting, and have department codes, department names, and the corresponding administrative department names, excluding the Management department?
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.COURSE) AS num_distinct_courses FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ad ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND UPPER(ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) <> 'MANAGEMENT' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY num_distinct_courses DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each academic year and department where the number of enrolled students in a subject is greater than 10 and the department is Chemistry, give the number of unique subjects and the minimum total units offered, but only include results where the minimum total units is greater than the overall minimum total units for all subjects offered by Chemistry or Biology departments. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT a.ACADEMIC_YEAR, s.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT s.SUBJECT_ID) AS subject_count, MIN(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS a JOIN TIP_DETAIL t ON a.TERM_CODE = t.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY s ON t.TERM_CODE = s.TERM_CODE WHERE s.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 10 AND s.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Chemistry' AND s.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology') GROUP BY a.ACADEMIC_YEAR, s.OFFER_DEPT_NAME ) SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR, OFFER_DEPT_NAME, subject_count, min_total_units FROM inner_cte WHERE min_total_units > ( SELECT MIN(s2.TOTAL_UNITS) FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY s2 WHERE s2.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology') );
domain_knowledge: "biology and chemistry department" is predicated by "TABLE.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology')"
sub_questions: For each academic year and department where the number of enrolled students in a subject is greater than 10 and the department is Chemistry, give the number of unique subjects and the minimum total units offered, but only include subjects that are offered by either the Chemistry or Biology departments.
sub_sqls: SELECT a.ACADEMIC_YEAR, s.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT s.SUBJECT_ID) AS subject_count, MIN(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS a JOIN TIP_DETAIL t ON a.TERM_CODE = t.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY s ON t.TERM_CODE = s.TERM_CODE WHERE s.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 10 AND s.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Chemistry' AND s.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology') GROUP BY a.ACADEMIC_YEAR, s.OFFER_DEPT_NAME;

question: From the top 10 departments with the highest number of graduate students whose department is degree-granting and whose department code is '17', display each department's name, total graduate student count, the most common subject code among those students, and the description of that subject code. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t2.FULL_NAME, t2.EMAIL_ADDRESS, t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY t2.FULL_NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE t0 JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY t2 ON t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t2.DEPARTMENT WHERE t2.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND t1.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '17' ) SELECT dept.DEPARTMENT_NAME, dept.Graduate_Student_Count, subj.SUBJECT_CODE AS Most_Common_Subject_Code, subj.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC FROM ( SELECT t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(t2.FULL_NAME) AS Graduate_Student_Count FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t1 JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY t2 ON t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t2.DEPARTMENT WHERE t2.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND t1.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '17' GROUP BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY Graduate_Student_Count DESC LIMIT 10 ) dept LEFT JOIN ( SELECT t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, COUNT(*) AS Subject_Count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rn FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE t0 JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY t2 ON t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t2.DEPARTMENT WHERE t2.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND t1.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '17' GROUP BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC ) subj ON dept.DEPARTMENT_NAME = subj.DEPARTMENT_NAME AND subj.rn = 1 ORDER BY dept.Graduate_Student_Count DESC;
sub_questions: For students whose year is 'G' and whose department is degree-granting and is 'Political Science', show their full name, email address, department name, and assign row numbers within a window of 2 preceding and 1 following rows ordered by full name, including the subject code and subject code description for each student's department, and only include students whose department code is '17'.
sub_sqls: SELECT t2.FULL_NAME, t2.EMAIL_ADDRESS, t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY t2.FULL_NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE t0 JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY t2 ON t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t2.DEPARTMENT WHERE t2.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND t1.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '17'

question: For each department, provide the department name, the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department, and the average number of enrolled students for those subjects, including only departments that have more than 5 subjects offered in the 2021FA term, excluding the Chemistry and Biology departments. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, sos.TOTAL_UNITS, sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sos.TERM_CODE = '2021FA' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE NOT IN ('5', '7') ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV(inner_cte.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units, AVG(inner_cte.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_num_enrolled_students FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, provide the department name, the standard deviation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, and include only departments that have more than 5 subjects offered in the 2021FA term, excluding the Chemistry and Biology departments.
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sos.TERM_CODE = '2021FA' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE NOT IN ('5', '7') GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(sos.SUBJECT_ID) > 5 ORDER BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding Mathematics and those with null full names), what is the department name, the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the CIP program codes for all courses in that department, and the corresponding SIS subject code and subject code description for each course? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_program_code_variance, STDDEV(scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_program_code_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = scd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '18' AND scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.cip_program_code_variance, inner_cte.cip_program_code_stddev, sc.SUBJECT_CODE, sc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC FROM inner_cte JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = scd.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE sc ON scd.COURSE = sc.COURSE_NUMBER WHERE scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE IS NOT NULL
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name, the variance, and the standard deviation of the CIP program codes for all courses in that department, considering only departments that grant degrees, have a non-null department full name, and are not the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_program_code_variance, STDDEV(scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS cip_program_code_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = scd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '18' AND scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE IS NOT NULL GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: For each department name and course level, where the total number of enrolled students in offered subjects is greater than 10, and the department is Mathematics (Course 18), provide the number of unique courses and the minimum total units among those subjects that are degree-granting courses. Additionally, show the school name for each department and indicate whether the minimum total units is above or below 12 (label as 'ABOVE_12' or 'BELOW_12'). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.COURSE_LEVEL, COUNT(DISTINCT c.COURSE) AS course_count, MIN(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE s.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 10 AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND c.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.COURSE_LEVEL ) SELECT i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.COURSE_LEVEL, i.course_count, i.min_total_units, d.SCHOOL_NAME, CASE WHEN i.min_total_units > 12 THEN 'ABOVE_12' ELSE 'BELOW_12' END AS unit_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON i.DEPARTMENT_NAME = d.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department name and course level, where the total number of enrolled students in offered subjects is greater than 10, and the department is Mathematics (Course 18), provide the number of unique courses and the minimum total units among those subjects that are degree-granting courses.
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.COURSE_LEVEL, COUNT(DISTINCT c.COURSE) AS course_count, MIN(s.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE s.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 10 AND d.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND c.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.COURSE_LEVEL;

question: For each department hierarchy level 2 that is not "Political Science", what is the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the organization numbers for organizations in that hierarchy level, excluding organizations with organization IDs '138' and '250'? Show the department hierarchy level 2 name and the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), but only for those hierarchy levels where the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) is greater than the overall average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all such hierarchy levels. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT mdh.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_NAME AS department_hierarchy_level_2, STDDEV_SAMP(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) / AVG(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY mdh JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT hou ON mdh.DLC_KEY = hou.DLC_KEY JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION fo ON hou.DLC_KEY = fo.DLC_KEY WHERE fo.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') AND mdh.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_NAME <> 'Political Science' GROUP BY mdh.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_NAME HAVING AVG(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) > 0 ) SELECT department_hierarchy_level_2, coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte WHERE coefficient_of_variation > (SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) FROM inner_cte);
domain_knowledge: "exclude organizations '138' and '250'" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250')"
sub_questions: For each department hierarchy level 2 that is not "Political Science", what is the coefficient of variation of the organization numbers for organizations in that hierarchy level, excluding organizations with organization IDs '138' and '250'? Show the department hierarchy level 2 name and the coefficient of variation, only for hierarchy levels where the average organization number is greater than zero.
sub_sqls: SELECT mdh.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_NAME AS department_hierarchy_level_2, STDDEV_SAMP(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) / AVG(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY mdh JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT hou ON mdh.DLC_KEY = hou.DLC_KEY JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION fo ON hou.DLC_KEY = fo.DLC_KEY WHERE fo.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') AND mdh.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_NAME <> 'Political Science' GROUP BY mdh.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_2_NAME HAVING AVG(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER) > 0

question: For each department, provide the department name, the average, range, and variance of the number of enrolled students in subjects offered by that department, considering only departments that grant degrees and subjects with at least one enrolled student. Additionally, for each school, include a grand total for all departments in that school in the format of (null department name, school name, nulls for statistics, and total enrolled students). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS >= 1 ), DepartmentStats AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrolled_students, MAX(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) - MIN(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS range_enrolled_students, VARIANCE(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS var_enrolled_students, SUM(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrolled_students FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME ), SchoolRollup AS ( SELECT NULL AS DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, NULL AS avg_enrolled_students, NULL AS range_enrolled_students, NULL AS var_enrolled_students, SUM(total_enrolled_students) AS total_enrolled_students FROM DepartmentStats GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, avg_enrolled_students, range_enrolled_students, var_enrolled_students, total_enrolled_students FROM DepartmentStats UNION ALL SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, avg_enrolled_students, range_enrolled_students, var_enrolled_students, total_enrolled_students FROM SchoolRollup ORDER BY SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME ;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and calculate the average, range, and variance of the number of enrolled students in subjects offered by that department, considering only departments that grant degrees, subjects with at least one enrolled student, and restricting the results to the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrolled_students, MAX(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) - MIN(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS range_enrolled_students, VARIANCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS var_enrolled_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS >= 1 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For each department that grants degrees, provide the department name, the variance, and the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units of subjects offered by that department, considering only subjects with more than zero total units, and restrict the results to the Mathematics department (Course 18), using a common table expression (CTE). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT * FROM inner_cte;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and both the variance and standard deviation of the total units of subjects offered by that department, considering only departments that grant degrees, subjects with more than zero total units, and restrict the results to the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY total_units_variance DESC;

question: For each department, provide the department name, the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units of subjects offered by that department (considering only departments that grant degrees and subjects with more than zero total units), and indicate whether the department is a 'HIGH_VARIANCE' (variance at least 20% greater than the average variance across all such departments), 'LOW_VARIANCE' (variance at least 20% less than the average), or 'AVERAGE' otherwise. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) , avg_var_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(total_units_variance) AS avg_variance FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.total_units_variance, i.total_units_stddev, CASE WHEN i.total_units_variance > a.avg_variance * 1.2 THEN 'HIGH_VARIANCE' WHEN i.total_units_variance < a.avg_variance * 0.8 THEN 'LOW_VARIANCE' ELSE 'AVERAGE' END AS variance_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_var_cte a ORDER BY i.total_units_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and both the variance and standard deviation of the total units of subjects offered by that department, considering only departments that grant degrees, subjects with more than zero total units, and restrict the results to the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance, STDDEV(SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY total_units_variance DESC;

question: For each degree-granting department that has offered more than 5 subjects, show the department's full name, the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of students enrolled in its offered subjects, and for each such subject, display the subject's code, title, and the number of enrolled students. Restrict the results to the Mathematics department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, STDDEV(TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN STUDENT_DEPARTMENT ON TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = STUDENT_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, inner_cte.enrolled_stddev, tso.SUBJECT_ID, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS FROM inner_cte JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE ORDER BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, tso.SUBJECT_ID;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department's full name and the standard deviation of the number of students enrolled in its offered subjects, considering only departments that have offered more than 5 subjects and are degree-granting, and restrict the results to the Mathematics department?
sub_sqls: SELECT SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, STDDEV(TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS enrolled_stddev FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN STUDENT_DEPARTMENT ON TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = STUDENT_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY enrolled_stddev DESC;

question: For each department that grants degrees, what is the department name, and what are the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units of courses offered by that department, considering only courses with a non-null total units value, and only include departments where the variance of total units is greater than the average variance across all degree-granting departments? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS variance_total_units, STDDEV(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccc.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, variance_total_units, stddev_total_units FROM inner_cte WHERE variance_total_units > ( SELECT AVG(variance_total_units) FROM inner_cte );
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name, and what are the variance and standard deviation of the total units of courses offered by that department, considering only courses with a non-null total units value and departments that grant degrees, specifically for the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS variance_total_units, STDDEV(ccc.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG ccc ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccc.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccc.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: For each school, provide the school name and the highest total clearing cost collector among its degree granting departments that have a department budget code greater than 100000, are not the Mathematics department, and are not the Physics department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME, SUM(sad.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS total_clearing_cost_collector FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE > 100000 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Mathematics' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '8' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, MAX(total_clearing_cost_collector) AS highest_total_clearing_cost_collector FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and calculate the total clearing cost collector for departments that are degree granting, have a department budget code greater than 100000, are not the Mathematics department, and are not the Physics department.
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(sad.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS total_clearing_cost_collector FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE > 100000 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Mathematics' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '8' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: For each building, provide the building name, the fiscal period, and the total area of rooms used for "RESIDENT" or "LABS" purposes, considering only buildings with a total room area greater than 1000, and only include buildings that are classified as "academic buildings" and are owned by MIT. For each fiscal period, include a grand total for all buildings in the format of (null, fiscal period, total room area). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fb.BUILDING_NAME, SUM(fr.AREA) AS total_room_area, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY FROM FCLT_ROOMS fr JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC IN ('RESIDENT', 'LABS') AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'OWNED' GROUP BY fb.BUILDING_NAME, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY HAVING SUM(fr.AREA) > 1000 ), BuildingPeriods AS ( SELECT ic.BUILDING_NAME, fbh.FISCAL_PERIOD, ic.total_room_area FROM inner_cte ic JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_HIST fbh ON ic.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ) SELECT bp.BUILDING_NAME, bp.FISCAL_PERIOD, SUM(bp.total_room_area) AS total_room_area FROM BuildingPeriods bp GROUP BY bp.FISCAL_PERIOD, bp.BUILDING_NAME WITH ROLLUP HAVING SUM(bp.total_room_area) > 0 ORDER BY bp.FISCAL_PERIOD, bp.BUILDING_NAME
sub_questions: For each building, give the building name and calculate the total area of rooms used for "RESIDENT" or "LABS" purposes, considering only buildings with a total room area greater than 1000, and only include buildings that are classified as "academic buildings" and are owned by MIT.
sub_sqls: SELECT fb.BUILDING_NAME, SUM(fr.AREA) AS total_room_area FROM FCLT_ROOMS fr JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC IN ('RESIDENT', 'LABS') AND fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'OWNED' GROUP BY fb.BUILDING_NAME HAVING total_room_area > 1000 ;

question: For each department in the 'Standard Hierarchy' whose name is 'Political Science', list the department name, the number of organizations associated with it (excluding organizations with IDs '138' and '250' and only those with a non-null description), and the average number of organizations per department in the 'Standard Hierarchy' (with the same filters). Also, indicate whether the department is an 'ABOVE_AVERAGE' performer (if its organization count is greater than the average), 'BELOW_AVERAGE' (if less), or 'AVERAGE' (if equal). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT m.DLC_NAME, COUNT(f.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS organization_count FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY m JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION f ON m.DLC_KEY = f.DLC_KEY JOIN FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY d ON f.DLC_KEY = d.DLC_KEY WHERE m.HIERARCHY_TYPE = 'Standard Hierarchy' AND f.DESCRIPTION IS NOT NULL AND m.DLC_NAME = 'Political Science' AND f.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') GROUP BY m.DLC_NAME ) , avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(org_count) AS avg_organization_count FROM ( SELECT m.DLC_NAME, COUNT(f.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS org_count FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY m JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION f ON m.DLC_KEY = f.DLC_KEY JOIN FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY d ON f.DLC_KEY = d.DLC_KEY WHERE m.HIERARCHY_TYPE = 'Standard Hierarchy' AND f.DESCRIPTION IS NOT NULL AND f.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') GROUP BY m.DLC_NAME ) sub ) SELECT i.DLC_NAME, i.organization_count, a.avg_organization_count, CASE WHEN i.organization_count > a.avg_organization_count THEN 'ABOVE_AVERAGE' WHEN i.organization_count < a.avg_organization_count THEN 'BELOW_AVERAGE' ELSE 'AVERAGE' END AS performance_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a;

sub_questions: List the top 10 department names along with the number of organizations associated with each, considering only departments that belong to the 'Standard Hierarchy', have a non-null description in their organizations, and excluding organizations with IDs '138' and '250'. Additionally, only include departments whose name is 'Political Science' (i.e., Course 17).
sub_sqls: SELECT m.DLC_NAME, COUNT(f.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS organization_count FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY m JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION f ON m.DLC_KEY = f.DLC_KEY JOIN FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY d ON f.DLC_KEY = d.DLC_KEY WHERE m.HIERARCHY_TYPE = 'Standard Hierarchy' AND f.DESCRIPTION IS NOT NULL AND m.DLC_NAME = 'Political Science' AND f.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') GROUP BY m.DLC_NAME ORDER BY organization_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding Chemistry), list the department name and the titles of subjects offered by that department where the number of enrolled students in the subject exceeds the average number of enrolled students for subjects in that department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '5' ), dept_avg AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE, AVG(NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrolled FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.SUBJECT_TITLE, i.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS FROM inner_cte i JOIN dept_avg d ON i.DEPARTMENT_CODE = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE i.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > d.avg_enrolled;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and find the average and standard deviation of the number of enrolled students in subjects offered by that department, considering only departments that are degree granting and are not the Chemistry department (Course 5).
