question: For each department, what is the department name and the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of enrolled students in the subjects it offers, but only include departments where this coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) is greater than the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all departments? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, (STDDEV_SAMP(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) / NULLIF(AVG(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS), 0)) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte WHERE coefficient_of_variation > (SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) FROM inner_cte);
sub_questions: For each department, what is the department name and the coefficient of variation of the number of enrolled students in the subjects it offers, considering only the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, (STDDEV_SAMP(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) / NULLIF(AVG(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS), 0)) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For subjects in the academic term with the term code '2019FA' that are in the Mathematics department, show the subject ID, subject title, department name, total units, the rank of each subject within its department (ordered by subject ID), and the deviation of each subject's total units from the average total units of all Mathematics subjects in that term. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t1.SUBJECT_ID, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.TOTAL_UNITS, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t1.SUBJECT_ID) AS window_column FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS t0 JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ), avg_units_cte AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units FROM SUBJECT_SUMMARY WHERE TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT i.SUBJECT_ID, i.SUBJECT_TITLE, i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.TOTAL_UNITS, i.window_column, (i.TOTAL_UNITS - a.avg_total_units) AS deviation_from_avg_units FROM inner_cte i JOIN avg_units_cte a ON i.DEPARTMENT_NAME = a.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For subjects in the academic term with the term code '2019FA' that are in the Mathematics department, show the subject ID, subject title, department name, total units, and the rank of each subject within its department (ordered by subject ID).
sub_sqls: SELECT t1.SUBJECT_ID, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.TOTAL_UNITS, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t1.SUBJECT_ID) AS window_column FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS t0 JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each department (excluding 'Biology'), list the department name, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department, and the subject with the highest total units in that department along with its total units. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department_name, (STDDEV_SAMP(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS), 0)) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED so ON sos.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON so.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID WHERE sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME <> 'Biology' GROUP BY sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ) SELECT ic.department_name, ic.coefficient_of_variation, ss2.SUBJECT_TITLE AS subject_with_max_units, ss2.TOTAL_UNITS AS max_total_units FROM inner_cte ic JOIN ( SELECT sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ss.SUBJECT_TITLE, ss.TOTAL_UNITS, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME ORDER BY ss.TOTAL_UNITS DESC) AS rn FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED so ON sos.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON so.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID WHERE sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME <> 'Biology' ) ss2 ON ic.department_name = ss2.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AND ss2.rn = 1 ORDER BY ic.department_name;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the coefficient of variation of the total units for subjects offered by that department, but only include departments that are not 'Biology' (Course 7).
sub_sqls: SELECT sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department_name, (STDDEV_SAMP(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ss.TOTAL_UNITS), 0)) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED so ON sos.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON so.SUBJECT_ID = ss.SUBJECT_ID WHERE sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME <> 'Biology' GROUP BY sos.OFFER_DEPT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ;

question: For each student year, provide the student year, the average, range, and variance of department budget codes for students in that year, considering only students whose department code matches both an academic department and an administrative department, and who are in the Mathematics department (Course 18). Additionally, include the total number of such students in each year. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR, SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ON MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT = SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' ) SELECT inner_cte.STUDENT_YEAR, AVG(inner_cte.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_budget, MAX(inner_cte.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(inner_cte.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_range, VARIANCE(inner_cte.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_variance, COUNT(*) AS num_students FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.STUDENT_YEAR ORDER BY budget_range DESC;
sub_questions: For each student year, give the student year and calculate the average, range, and variance of department budget codes for students in that year, considering only students whose department code matches both an academic department and an administrative department, and who are in the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR, AVG(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_budget, MAX(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_range, VARIANCE(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ON MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT = SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR ORDER BY budget_range DESC;

question: For each organization, what is the highest geometric mean of the old department codes for all associated HR organization units, grouped by the organization and the HR org unit level, where the old department code is greater than zero, excluding organizations '138' and '250', and only for organizations that are not 'CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST'? Show the organization name, HR org unit level, and the highest geometric mean per organization. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NAME, HR_ORG_UNIT.HR_ORG_UNIT_LEVEL, EXP(AVG(LN(HR_ORG_UNIT.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD))) AS geometric_mean FROM FCLT_ORGANIZATION JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT ON FCLT_ORGANIZATION.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = HR_ORG_UNIT.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID WHERE HR_ORG_UNIT.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD > 0 AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NAME NOT IN ('CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST') GROUP BY FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NAME, HR_ORG_UNIT.HR_ORG_UNIT_LEVEL ) SELECT ORGANIZATION_NAME, HR_ORG_UNIT_LEVEL, MAX(geometric_mean) AS highest_geometric_mean FROM inner_cte GROUP BY ORGANIZATION_NAME, HR_ORG_UNIT_LEVEL ORDER BY highest_geometric_mean DESC;
domain_knowledge: "exclude organizations '138' and '250'" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250')"
"except Cambridge-MIT Institute" is predicated by "TABLE.ORGANIZATION_NAME NOT IN ('CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST')"
sub_questions: For each organization, what is the geometric mean of the old department codes for all associated HR organization units where the old department code is greater than zero, excluding organizations '138' and '250', and only for organizations that are not 'CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST'? Show the organization name and the geometric mean.
sub_sqls: SELECT FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NAME, EXP(AVG(LN(HR_ORG_UNIT.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD))) AS geometric_mean FROM FCLT_ORGANIZATION JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT ON FCLT_ORGANIZATION.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = HR_ORG_UNIT.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID WHERE HR_ORG_UNIT.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD > 0 AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_ID NOT IN ('138', '250') AND FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NAME NOT IN ('CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST') GROUP BY FCLT_ORGANIZATION.ORGANIZATION_NAME ORDER BY geometric_mean DESC;

question: For each school, list its name, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by degree-granting departments in the 2022 academic year (excluding the 'Political Science' department), and the number of such departments in the school. For each school, also include a grand total row in the format (school name, null, total departments). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ), SchoolStats AS ( SELECT sd.SCHOOL_NAME, ic.coefficient_of_variation, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ), SchoolAgg AS ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation, COUNT(DISTINCT DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS num_departments FROM SchoolStats GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, avg_coefficient_of_variation, num_departments FROM SchoolAgg UNION ALL SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, NULL, SUM(num_departments) FROM SchoolAgg GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY SCHOOL_NAME, avg_coefficient_of_variation
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the coefficient of variation of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the 2022 academic year, but only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the 'Political Science' department.
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, STDDEV_SAMP(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Political Science' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0

question: For each degree-granting department with a department budget code greater than 100000, excluding the Mathematics and Physics departments, provide the department name, the total clearing cost collector, and the department's school name. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(sad.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS total_clearing_cost_collector, sd.SCHOOL_NAME FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE > 100000 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Mathematics' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '8' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.total_clearing_cost_collector, ic.SCHOOL_NAME FROM inner_cte ic;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and calculate the total clearing cost collector for departments that are degree granting, have a department budget code greater than 100000, are not the Mathematics department, and are not the Physics department.
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(sad.CLEARING_COST_COLLECTOR) AS total_clearing_cost_collector FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT sad ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE > 100000 AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Mathematics' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '8' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ;

question: For each subject code where the department is degree granting and the department is Mathematics, show the subject code, subject code description, department name, school name, and the number of subject codes per school, as well as a grand total of subject codes per school in the format (school name, null, total subject codes). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t1.SUBJECT_CODE, t1.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.SCHOOL_NAME FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE t1 ON t0.SCHOOL_CODE = t1.SCHOOL_CODE WHERE t0.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ), SubjectCodeCounts AS ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE, SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(*) AS subject_code_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE, SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, DEPARTMENT_NAME ), RollupResults AS ( SELECT SCHOOL_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE, SUM(subject_code_count) AS total_subject_codes FROM SubjectCodeCounts GROUP BY SCHOOL_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE WITH ROLLUP HAVING SUM(subject_code_count) > 0 ) SELECT rr.SCHOOL_NAME, rr.SUBJECT_CODE, rr.total_subject_codes FROM RollupResults rr ORDER BY rr.SCHOOL_NAME, rr.SUBJECT_CODE
sub_questions: For each subject code where the department is degree granting and the department is Mathematics, show the subject code, subject code description, department name, school name, and rank of the subject code within each school name group ordered by subject code.
sub_sqls: SELECT t1.SUBJECT_CODE, t1.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.SCHOOL_NAME, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY t1.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE t1 ON t0.SCHOOL_CODE = t1.SCHOOL_CODE WHERE t0.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each type of space usage in the Stata building, what is the name of the space usage and the variance of the square footage of rooms used for that purpose, considering only rooms with more than 10 square feet and excluding usage types that include 'STORAGE', and only include those space usage types where the variance is greater than the average variance across all such usage types in the Stata building? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT su.SPACE_USAGE, VARIANCE(sd.ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS variance_square_footage FROM SPACE_DETAIL sd JOIN SPACE_USAGE su ON sd.SPACE_USAGE_KEY = su.SPACE_USAGE_KEY WHERE sd.BUILDING_KEY = '32' AND sd.ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE > 10 AND su.SPACE_USAGE NOT LIKE '%STORAGE%' GROUP BY su.SPACE_USAGE ) SELECT SPACE_USAGE, variance_square_footage FROM inner_cte WHERE variance_square_footage > ( SELECT AVG(variance_square_footage) FROM inner_cte );
domain_knowledge: "exclude usage types that include 'STORAGE'" is predicated by "TABLE.SPACE_USAGE NOT LIKE '%STORAGE%'"
sub_questions: For each type of space usage, what is the name of the space usage and the variance of the square footage of rooms used for that purpose in the Stata building, considering only rooms with more than 10 square feet and excluding usage types that include 'STORAGE'?
sub_sqls: SELECT su.SPACE_USAGE, VARIANCE(sd.ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS variance_square_footage FROM SPACE_DETAIL sd JOIN SPACE_USAGE su ON sd.SPACE_USAGE_KEY = su.SPACE_USAGE_KEY WHERE sd.BUILDING_KEY = '32' AND sd.ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE > 10 AND su.SPACE_USAGE NOT LIKE '%STORAGE%' GROUP BY su.SPACE_USAGE;

question: For each degree-granting department, what is the maximum number of students enrolled in any subject offered by that department in the 2019FA term, what is the title of the subject with that maximum enrollment, and is the department a 'HIGH_ENROLLMENT' department (if the maximum enrollment is at least 20% greater than the average maximum enrollment across all degree-granting departments), a 'LOW_ENROLLMENT' department (if the maximum enrollment is at least 20% less than the average), or 'AVERAGE'? Only include departments where the maximum enrollment is greater than 10. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS AS MAX_NUM_ENROLLED FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS = ( SELECT MAX(tso2.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso2 WHERE tso2.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE AND tso2.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' ) AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 10 ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.SUBJECT_TITLE, ic.MAX_NUM_ENROLLED, CASE WHEN ic.MAX_NUM_ENROLLED > avg_stats.avg_max_enrolled * 1.2 THEN 'HIGH_ENROLLMENT' WHEN ic.MAX_NUM_ENROLLED < avg_stats.avg_max_enrolled * 0.8 THEN 'LOW_ENROLLMENT' ELSE 'AVERAGE' END AS enrollment_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN ( SELECT AVG(MAX_NUM_ENROLLED) AS avg_max_enrolled FROM inner_cte ) avg_stats;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the maximum number of students enrolled in any subject offered by that department in the 2019FA term, and what is the title of the subject with that maximum enrollment, considering only departments that are degree granting, where the maximum enrollment is greater than 10, and restricting to the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS AS MAX_NUM_ENROLLED FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS = ( SELECT MAX(tso2.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso2 WHERE tso2.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE AND tso2.TERM_CODE = '2019FA' ) AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 10 ;

question: For each department, what is the maximum CIP program code among its courses, the full name of the department, and the school name, for departments that grant degrees, have a maximum CIP program code greater than 120000, and are not the Mathematics department (Course 18)? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS max_cip_code, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME HAVING MAX(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) > 120000 ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.max_cip_code, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, sd.SCHOOL_NAME FROM inner_cte LEFT JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the maximum CIP program code among its courses, and what is the full name of the department, for departments that grant degrees, have a maximum CIP program code greater than 120000, and are not the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS max_cip_code, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME HAVING MAX(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) > 120000;

question: For each degree-granting department (excluding the Biology department), show the department name, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the most recent academic year (for departments with more than one subject), and for each such department, list the subject codes and subject code descriptions for the subjects included in the calculation. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH most_recent_year AS ( SELECT MAX(ACADEMIC_YEAR) AS max_year FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ), dept_units AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ccs.TOTAL_UNITS, ccs.SUBJECT_CODE FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccs JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '7' AND ccs.ACADEMIC_YEAR = (SELECT max_year FROM most_recent_year) AND ccs.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE, TOTAL_UNITS FROM dept_units ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, (STDDEV(ic.TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(ic.TOTAL_UNITS), 0)) AS coefficient_of_variation, sc.SUBJECT_CODE, sc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE sc ON ic.SUBJECT_CODE = sc.SUBJECT_CODE GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sc.SUBJECT_CODE, sc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sc.SUBJECT_CODE;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the coefficient of variation of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the most recent academic year, but only include departments that are degree-granting and exclude the Biology department (Course 7).
sub_sqls: WITH most_recent_year AS ( SELECT MAX(ACADEMIC_YEAR) AS max_year FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ), dept_units AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ccs.TOTAL_UNITS FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccs JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '7' AND ccs.ACADEMIC_YEAR = (SELECT max_year FROM most_recent_year) AND ccs.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, (STDDEV(TOTAL_UNITS) / NULLIF(AVG(TOTAL_UNITS), 0)) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM dept_units GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_NAME;

question: For each academic year, give the academic year, the academic year description, and find the highest average total units for subjects that are offered in the fall term, have a material status of 'U' in the library reserve, and are offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18), grouped by department. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units FROM LIBRARY_RESERVE_MATRL_DETAIL lrm JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON lrm.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON at.TERM_CODE = ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE lrm.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = 'U' AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ccso.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, MAX(avg_total_units) AS highest_avg_total_units FROM inner_cte GROUP BY ACADEMIC_YEAR, ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ORDER BY ACADEMIC_YEAR;
sub_questions: For each academic year, give the academic year, the academic year description and find the average and standard deviation of the total units for subjects that are offered in the fall term, have a material status of 'U' in the library reserve, and are offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, AVG(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS avg_total_units, STDDEV(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS stddev_total_units FROM LIBRARY_RESERVE_MATRL_DETAIL lrm JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON lrm.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON at.TERM_CODE = ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE lrm.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = 'U' AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ccso.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ORDER BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR

question: For each subject offered in the 2022 academic year by a degree-granting department, specifically in the Department of Mathematics (Course 18) but not in the Department of Physics, provide the subject ID, subject title, department name, the number of enrolled students, the total number of lecture units, and the name of the responsible faculty member. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT tso.SUBJECT_ID, ccso.SUBJECT_TITLE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, ccso.LECTURE_UNITS FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON tso.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Physics' ) SELECT i.SUBJECT_ID, i.SUBJECT_TITLE, i.DEPARTMENT_NAME, i.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, i.LECTURE_UNITS, ccso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME FROM inner_cte i JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON i.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022;
sub_questions: For each subject offered in the 2022 academic year by a degree-granting department, specifically in the Department of Mathematics (Course 18), provide the subject ID, subject title, department name, the number of enrolled students, and the total number of lecture units, but exclude subjects offered by the Department of Physics.
sub_sqls: SELECT tso.SUBJECT_ID, ccso.SUBJECT_TITLE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, ccso.LECTURE_UNITS FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON tso.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID AND ccso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME <> 'Physics'

question: For each degree-granting department in the School of Engineering (excluding the Department of Management, Course 15), what is the maximum total units of any course offered by that department in the 2008 academic year, and what is the subject code of that course? Only include departments where this maximum total units is greater than the average maximum total units across all such departments. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units, c.SUBJECT_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG c ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = c.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND c.ACADEMIC_YEAR = '2008' AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '15' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.SUBJECT_CODE HAVING MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0 ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, max_total_units, SUBJECT_CODE FROM inner_cte WHERE max_total_units > ( SELECT AVG(max_total_units) FROM inner_cte );
sub_questions: For each department in the School of Engineering that is degree-granting, what is the maximum total units of any course offered by that department in the 2008 academic year, and what is the subject code of that course? Exclude the Department of Management (Course 15) from the results.
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units, c.SUBJECT_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT d JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG c ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = c.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE s ON c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' AND c.ACADEMIC_YEAR = '2008' AND d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '15' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.SUBJECT_CODE HAVING MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) > 0;

question: For subjects offered in the academic year 2024 with a total of 12 units in the Mathematics department (Course 18), show the subject code, subject title, department name, school name, and, for each department, the number of such subjects and a grand total per school. Display the department name, school name, subject code, subject title, and the count of subjects, including a subtotal for each department and a grand total for each school. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t1.SUBJECT_CODE, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SCHOOL_NAME FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t1.TOTAL_UNITS = 12 AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ), DeptSchoolRollup AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE, SUBJECT_TITLE, COUNT(*) AS subject_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE, SUBJECT_TITLE WITH ROLLUP HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, SCHOOL_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE, SUBJECT_TITLE, subject_count FROM DeptSchoolRollup ORDER BY SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUBJECT_CODE
sub_questions: For subjects offered in the academic year 2024 with a total of 12 units in the Mathematics department (Course 18), show the subject code, subject title, department name, school name, and rank within each school name group ordered by subject code.
sub_sqls: SELECT t1.SUBJECT_CODE, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SCHOOL_NAME, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY t1.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t1.TOTAL_UNITS = 12 AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each student year, list the student year, the average, range, and variance of department budget codes for students in that year whose department code matches both an academic department and an administrative department, and who are in the Mathematics department (Course 18). Additionally, for each student year, include a grand total row for all years in the format of (null, total average, total range, total variance). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR, SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ON MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT = SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' ) SELECT STUDENT_YEAR, AVG(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_budget, MAX(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_range, VARIANCE(DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_variance FROM inner_cte GROUP BY STUDENT_YEAR WITH ROLLUP HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 ORDER BY CASE WHEN STUDENT_YEAR IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, budget_range DESC;
sub_questions: For each student year, give the student year and calculate the average, range, and variance of department budget codes for students in that year, considering only students whose department code matches both an academic department and an administrative department, and who are in the Mathematics department (Course 18).
sub_sqls: SELECT MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR, AVG(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS avg_budget, MAX(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) - MIN(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_range, VARIANCE(SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE) AS budget_variance FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY ON SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ON MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.DEPARTMENT = SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE IS NOT NULL AND SIS_DEPARTMENT.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' GROUP BY MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY.STUDENT_YEAR ORDER BY budget_range DESC;

question: For each organization, what is the highest HR department code (old) among its associated HR org units, what is the HR department name, and what is the corresponding HR org unit title, considering only organizations whose highest HR department code (old) is greater than 500000, and excluding organizations named 'ADMISSIONS'? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, MAX(hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD) AS max_hr_dept_code_old, hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY fodk JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION fo ON fodk.DLC_KEY = fo.DLC_KEY JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT hou ON fo.DLC_KEY = hou.DLC_KEY WHERE fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME <> 'ADMISSIONS' GROUP BY fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING MAX(hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD) > 500000 ) SELECT ic.ORGANIZATION_NAME, ic.max_hr_dept_code_old, ic.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, hou.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE FROM inner_cte ic JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT hou ON ic.max_hr_dept_code_old = hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD AND ic.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME = hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
sub_questions: For each organization, what is the highest HR department code (old) among its associated HR org units, and what is the HR department name, considering only organizations whose highest HR department code (old) is greater than 500000, and excluding organizations named 'ADMISSIONS'?
sub_sqls: SELECT fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, MAX(hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD) AS max_hr_dept_code_old, hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME FROM FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY fodk JOIN FCLT_ORGANIZATION fo ON fodk.DLC_KEY = fo.DLC_KEY JOIN HR_ORG_UNIT hou ON fo.DLC_KEY = hou.DLC_KEY WHERE fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME <> 'ADMISSIONS' GROUP BY fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING MAX(hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD) > 500000;

question: Which are the top 3 degree-granting departments (excluding Management) that offer the most distinct courses, and for each, what is the department code, department name, administrative department name, and the total number of courses offered at the undergraduate level? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.COURSE) AS num_distinct_courses FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ad ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND UPPER(ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) <> 'MANAGEMENT' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY num_distinct_courses DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(c.COURSE) AS num_undergrad_courses FROM inner_cte ic JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c ON ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE = c.DEPARTMENT WHERE c.COURSE_LEVEL = 'U' GROUP BY ic.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ic.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ic.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY num_undergrad_courses DESC;
sub_questions: Which are the top 3 departments that offer the most distinct courses, are degree-granting, and have department codes, department names, and the corresponding administrative department names, excluding the Management department?
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.COURSE) AS num_distinct_courses FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ad ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND UPPER(ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME) <> 'MANAGEMENT' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_CODE, d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY num_distinct_courses DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each department that grants degrees (excluding the Biology department), what is the variance of the total units for subjects offered by that department in 2022, and how does this variance compare to the average variance across all such departments? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '7' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.total_units_variance, (inner_cte.total_units_variance - avg_variance.avg_total_units_variance) AS deviation_from_avg_variance FROM inner_cte CROSS JOIN ( SELECT AVG(total_units_variance) AS avg_total_units_variance FROM inner_cte ) avg_variance ORDER BY deviation_from_avg_variance DESC;
sub_questions: For each department, give the department name and the variance of the total units for subjects offered by that department in the year 2022, but only include departments that grant degrees and exclude the Biology department (Course 7).
sub_sqls: SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, VARIANCE(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_variance FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '7' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY total_units_variance DESC;

question: For students whose department name is 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' (Course 6), and whose first name is 'Kevin', show their full name, email address, student year, the department's full name, the course description, the course level, and whether the course level is 'GRADUATE' (if the course level is 'G'), 'UNDERGRADUATE' (if the course level is 'U'), or 'OTHER'. sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t2.FULL_NAME, t2.EMAIL_ADDRESS, t2.STUDENT_YEAR, t1.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, t0.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, t0.COURSE_LEVEL FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION t0 JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY t2 ON t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t2.DEPARTMENT WHERE t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' AND t2.FIRST_NAME = 'Kevin' AND t2.DEPARTMENT = '6' ) SELECT inner_cte.FULL_NAME, inner_cte.EMAIL_ADDRESS, inner_cte.STUDENT_YEAR, inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, inner_cte.COURSE_DESCRIPTION, inner_cte.COURSE_LEVEL, CASE WHEN inner_cte.COURSE_LEVEL = 'G' THEN 'GRADUATE' WHEN inner_cte.COURSE_LEVEL = 'U' THEN 'UNDERGRADUATE' ELSE 'OTHER' END AS course_level_category FROM inner_cte;

question: For each department, what is the range and variance of facility organization keys associated with it, and for each department hierarchy level 3, what are the total number of unique facility organization keys across all departments in that level, excluding the Political Science department? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT mdh.DLC_NAME AS department, mdh.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_3_NAME AS dept_level_3, MAX(fodk.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) - MIN(fodk.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS org_key_range, VARIANCE(fodk.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS org_key_variance FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY mdh JOIN FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY fodk ON mdh.DLC_KEY = fodk.DLC_KEY WHERE mdh.DLC_NAME <> 'Political Science' GROUP BY mdh.DLC_NAME, mdh.MASTER_DEPT_HIER_LEVEL_3_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.dept_level_3, inner_cte.department, inner_cte.org_key_range, inner_cte.org_key_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT fodk.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS total_unique_org_keys_in_level_3 FROM inner_cte JOIN MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY mdh ON inner_cte.department = mdh.DLC_NAME JOIN FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY fodk ON mdh.DLC_KEY = fodk.DLC_KEY GROUP BY inner_cte.dept_level_3, inner_cte.department, inner_cte.org_key_range, inner_cte.org_key_variance ORDER BY inner_cte.dept_level_3, inner_cte.department;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the range and variance of facility organization keys associated with it, excluding the Political Science department?
sub_sqls: SELECT mdh.DLC_NAME AS department, MAX(fodk.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) - MIN(fodk.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS org_key_range, VARIANCE(fodk.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS org_key_variance FROM MASTER_DEPT_HIERARCHY mdh JOIN FCLT_ORG_DLC_KEY fodk ON mdh.DLC_KEY = fodk.DLC_KEY WHERE mdh.DLC_NAME <> 'Political Science' GROUP BY mdh.DLC_NAME ORDER BY mdh.DLC_NAME;

question: For each academic building at MIT with building numbers between '14' and 'E62' or floor numbers at least 2, and floor numbers between 3 and 16, what are the minimum building number, average floor number, and the street name and city of the building's address? Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT fb.BUILDING_NUMBER, MIN(fb.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS min_building_number, AVG(ff.FLOOR) AS avg_floor_number, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY FROM FCLT_BUILDING fb JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.SITE = 'MIT' AND ( (fb.BUILDING_NUMBER >= '14' AND fb.BUILDING_NUMBER <= 'E62') OR ff.FLOOR >= 2 ) AND ff.FLOOR BETWEEN 3 AND 16 GROUP BY fb.BUILDING_NUMBER, fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ) SELECT ic.BUILDING_NUMBER, ic.min_building_number, ic.avg_floor_number, fba.STREET_NAME, fba.CITY FROM inner_cte ic JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba ON ic.BUILDING_NUMBER = fba.BUILDING_NUMBER ORDER BY ic.BUILDING_NUMBER;
sub_questions: What are the minimum building number and average floor number for each building that is an academic building, where building numbers are between '14' and 'E62' or floor numbers are at least 2, and floor numbers are between 3 and 16, and the building is at MIT?
sub_sqls: SELECT fb.BUILDING_NUMBER, MIN(fb.BUILDING_NUMBER) AS min_building_number, AVG(ff.FLOOR) AS avg_floor_number FROM FCLT_BUILDING fb JOIN FCLT_FLOOR ff ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'ACADEMIC' AND fb.SITE = 'MIT' AND ( (fb.BUILDING_NUMBER >= '14' AND fb.BUILDING_NUMBER <= 'E62') OR ff.FLOOR >= 2 ) AND ff.FLOOR BETWEEN 3 AND 16 GROUP BY fb.BUILDING_NUMBER ORDER BY fb.BUILDING_NUMBER ;

question: For each department, provide the department name, the average, range, and variance of the number of students enrolled in subjects offered by that department, as well as the total number of subjects offered, considering only departments that grant degrees, subjects with at least one enrolled student, and excluding the Chemistry department (Course 5). sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, AVG(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrolled, MAX(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) - MIN(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS range_enrolled, VARIANCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS var_enrolled FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS >= 1 AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME <> 'Chemistry' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.avg_enrolled, inner_cte.range_enrolled, inner_cte.var_enrolled, COUNT(tso.SUBJECT_ID) AS total_subjects_offered FROM inner_cte JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS >= 1 AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME <> 'Chemistry' GROUP BY inner_cte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, inner_cte.avg_enrolled, inner_cte.range_enrolled, inner_cte.var_enrolled

question: For each department that grants degrees and is not the Mathematics department (Course 18), and whose maximum CIP program code among its courses is greater than 120000, show the department's full name, the maximum CIP program code, the corresponding SIS subject code, the subject code description, and the graduate level for each course with that maximum CIP program code. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS max_cip_code, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME HAVING MAX(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) > 120000 ) SELECT icte.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, icte.max_cip_code, sc.SUBJECT_CODE, sc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC, scd.GRADUATE_LEVEL FROM inner_cte icte JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = d.DEPARTMENT_NAME JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = scd.DEPARTMENT AND scd.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE = icte.max_cip_code JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE sc ON scd.COURSE = sc.COURSE_NUMBER;
sub_questions: For each department, what is the maximum CIP program code among its courses, and what is the full name of the department, for departments that grant degrees, have a maximum CIP program code greater than 120000, and are not the Mathematics department (Course 18)?
sub_sqls: SELECT d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) AS max_cip_code, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME FROM SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE d.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND d.DEPARTMENT_CODE <> '18' GROUP BY d.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME HAVING MAX(c.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE) > 120000;

question: For each department, provide the department code, department name, and the total number of enrolled students in all subjects offered by that department, considering only those departments where the total number of enrolled students is more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the average total enrolled students across all departments, and restrict your answer to the Mathematics department (Course 18). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrolled_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc ON ssc.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE, sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING SUM(sos.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) > ( SELECT AVG(total_enrolled) + STDDEV(total_enrolled) FROM ( SELECT SUM(sos2.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrolled FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd2 JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos2 ON sd2.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sos2.OFFER_DEPT_CODE JOIN SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc2 ON ssc2.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd2.DEPARTMENT_CODE GROUP BY sd2.DEPARTMENT_CODE ) t ) ) SELECT DEPARTMENT_CODE, DEPARTMENT_NAME, total_enrolled_students FROM inner_cte;
